// D:\workspace\Fanan_web_hub\src\MidiLink.h

#pragma once

#include <juce_audio_basics/juce_audio_basics.h>
#include <juce_events/juce_events.h>

#include <functional>
#include <map>
#include <optional>
#include <utility>
#include <vector>

//==============================================================================
/**
    MIDI Link, as in Grex: move a knob, slider or wheel on a MIDI device (or hit a pad on a
    controller) and it shows as a chip in the toolbar's MIDI Link strip, the last six newest
    first. Drag the chip onto one of Sonify's controls (or tap the chip, then the control) and
    the device moves that control from then on:
        Push     the control is on while the button or pad is held
        Toggle   each press switches it on or off
        Knob     it follows the knob, slider or wheel
    Buttons take Push or Toggle, faders and knobs take Knob. A plugin's own knobs link through
    the strip's Last Touched slot: touch the knob in the plugin's window, then drop the chip there.

    One source moves one control: linking it again takes it from the control it moved. What a
    linked source sends reaches no track (the engine keeps it back).

    The map belongs to the setup, not the song, as Grex's: the same in every song, kept next to
    Sonify's settings, and saved to and loaded from files of its own. So controls are named by
    where they are: "track.2.volume" is the second track's fader in any song, "fx.1.pan" the first
    FX channel's pan. A plugin's parameter is named by the plugin and the parameter's id, and
    moves the selected track's copy of that plugin (or the first one in the song).

    Message thread.
*/
class MidiLink final : private juce::Timer
{
public:
    //==============================================================================
    enum class Kind { cc, note, pitchBend };
    enum class Mode { push, toggle, knob };

    /** Where a link comes from: a controller, a note or the pitch wheel, on a channel of a port. */
    struct Source
    {
        juce::String port;                  // the MIDI port it comes in on, by name
        Kind kind = Kind::cc;
        int channel = 1;                    // 1 .. 16
        int number = 0;                     // the controller or the note; 0 for pitch bend

        /** "cc|1|74|Port Name": what the page and the files name it by. */
        juce::String key() const;
        static std::optional<Source> fromKey (const juce::String& key);

        /** "CC 74", "C4" (middle C, as the Editor names it) or "Pitch Bend". */
        juce::String label() const;

        bool operator== (const Source& other) const noexcept;
        bool operator!= (const Source& other) const noexcept     { return ! operator== (other); }
    };

    /** What a link moves. key is one of:
            track.<n>.volume|pan|mute|solo|arm|monitor|send.<k>   the n-th track (as numbered)
            fx.<n>.volume|pan|mute|solo|send.<k>                  the n-th FX channel
            bus.<n>.volume|pan|mute|solo|send.<k>                 the n-th bus
            main.volume|mute
            board.<n>.<setting>, board.master.<setting>           the Analog Board: the n-th track's strip, its master
            live.deck.<n>.<setting>|play|cue|sync|hotcue<k>|loop<beats>, live.channel.<n>.<setting>,
            live.master.<setting>, live.pad.<n>, live.onair, live.record,  the Live Show: a deck (1 .. 4),
            live.mutemics, live.muteplayback (live.mute: both)       its n-th channel, its mixer, a pad,
                                                                  Enable streaming, REC and its mutes
            transport.play|stop|record|loop|metronome|start       start: back to the song's start
            plugin                                                a plugin's parameter (below) */
    struct Target
    {
        juce::String key;
        juce::String pluginId, pluginName, paramName;   // "plugin": the plugin's id and its parameter
        juce::uint32 paramId = 0;

        /** key, or "plugin|<pluginId>|<paramId>": one id per control. */
        juce::String id() const;

        /** A fader or a knob (Knob mode); the rest are buttons. */
        bool isContinuous() const;

        /** Something Sonify has (a well-formed key). */
        bool isValid() const;

        juce::var toVar() const;
        static Target fromVar (const juce::var& value);
    };

    struct Link
    {
        Source source;
        Target target;
        Mode mode = Mode::knob;
    };

    /** Sonify, as MIDI Link moves it. Message thread. */
    class Host
    {
    public:
        virtual ~Host() = default;

        /** A fader or knob to a position: 0 (all the way down, or left) .. 1. */
        virtual void linkMove (const Target& target, float position) = 0;

        /** A button on or off (start and stop act on "on"). */
        virtual void linkSet (const Target& target, bool on) = 0;

        /** Whether a button is on now (Toggle switches it the other way). */
        virtual bool linkIsOn (const Target& target) = 0;
    };

    using Message = std::pair<juce::String, juce::MidiMessage>;   // the port it came in on, and it
    using TakeIncoming = std::function<void (std::vector<Message>& into)>;

    /** takeIncoming hands over what came in since the last time; it's asked 60 times a second.
        None: messages come only through receive(). */
    MidiLink (Host& host, TakeIncoming takeIncoming);
    ~MidiLink() override;

    //==============================================================================
    /** The devices in Settings > MIDI Setup: the names chips show for their ports, and the ports
        whose notes are pads (a controller's): only those notes become chips, so playing a
        keyboard doesn't fill the strip. */
    void setDevices (std::map<juce::String, juce::String> deviceNamesByPort, juce::StringArray padPorts);
    juce::String deviceOf (const juce::String& port) const;

    /** A message from a port: it becomes the newest chip, and plays its link if it has one. */
    void receive (const juce::String& port, const juce::MidiMessage& message);

    //==============================================================================
    // The strip's chips: the sources that sent last, newest first.
    struct Recent
    {
        Source source;
        float value = 0.0f;                 // 0 .. 1, as it last sent
    };

    static constexpr size_t maxRecent = 6;
    const std::vector<Recent>& getRecent() const noexcept      { return recent; }

    //==============================================================================
    // The links.
    const std::vector<Link>& getLinks() const noexcept         { return links; }
    const Link* findLink (const Source& source) const;

    /** Links the source to the target, taking it from any control it moved. A note can't move a
        fader (false); a fader moves in Knob mode, a button in Push or Toggle (the mode is set to
        fit). */
    bool link (const Source& source, const Target& target, Mode mode);

    bool setMode (const Source& source, Mode mode);
    void unlinkTarget (const juce::String& targetId);   // every link to that control
    void clear();
    void setLinks (std::vector<Link> newLinks);          // as they were (Cancel), or loaded

    /** The mode a new link to this target starts in: Knob for a fader, Toggle for a button. */
    static Mode defaultModeFor (const Target& target);

    //==============================================================================
    // Files: the map kept next to Sonify's settings (saved at every change once it's set), and
    // maps saved by name (.sonifylink).
    juce::var toVar() const;
    juce::Result fromVar (const juce::var& value);     // links from a file; fails if it isn't a map
    bool save (const juce::File& file) const;
    juce::Result load (const juce::File& file);

    void setAutoFile (const juce::File& file)                  { autoFile = file; }
    static juce::File getDefaultAutoFile();                    // midilink.json, with Sonify's other settings
    static juce::File getMapsFolder();                         // <user data>\MIDI Link
    static constexpr const char* fileExtension = ".sonifylink";

    //==============================================================================
    /** The links changed: the engine keeps their sources from the tracks. */
    std::function<void (const std::vector<Source>&)> onLinkedSourcesChanged;

    /** Asked first of every message that comes in: true when another part of Sonify takes it
        (the Live Show's Controller: its pads, or one it's learning), and then it makes no chip
        and plays no link. */
    std::function<bool (const juce::String& port, const juce::MidiMessage& message)> claim;

    /** True once after something the strip shows changed: a new chip, a chip moved to the
        front, or the links. A chip's value alone isn't a change. */
    bool takeChanged() noexcept                                { return std::exchange (stripChanged, false); }

    static juce::String modeName (Mode mode);                  // "push", "toggle", "knob"
    static Mode modeFromName (const juce::String& name, Mode fallback);

private:
    void timerCallback() override;
    void linksChanged();

    Host& host;
    TakeIncoming takeIncoming;
    std::vector<Message> incoming;
    std::vector<Recent> recent;
    std::vector<Link> links;
    std::vector<bool> held;                     // per link: its button or pad is down now
    std::map<juce::String, juce::String> deviceNames;
    juce::StringArray padPorts;
    juce::File autoFile;
    bool stripChanged = false;

    JUCE_DECLARE_NON_COPYABLE_WITH_LEAK_DETECTOR (MidiLink)
};

// D:\workspace\Fanan_web_hub\src\MidiSync.cpp

#include "MidiSync.h"

#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>

namespace
{
    constexpr double ticksPerQuarter = 24.0;   // MIDI clock
    constexpr double epsilon = 1.0e-9;
}

//==============================================================================
/** Messages for one block, written into the caller's array. */
struct MidiSync::Planner::Out
{
    Message* messages = nullptr;
    int capacity = 0;
    int count = 0;

    void add (double time, juce::uint32 targets, std::initializer_list<juce::uint8> bytes) noexcept
    {
        if (targets == 0 || count >= capacity)
            return;

        auto& message = messages[count++];
        message.time = time;
        message.targets = targets;
        message.size = 0;

        for (const auto byte : bytes)
            if (message.size < static_cast<int> (message.bytes.size()))
                message.bytes[static_cast<size_t> (message.size++)] = byte;
    }

    /** Song Position Pointer: where the song is, in sixteenth notes. */
    void songPosition (double time, juce::uint32 targets, double ppq) noexcept
    {
        const auto sixteenths = juce::jlimit (0, 16383, static_cast<int> (std::floor (ppq * 4.0 + 1.0e-6)));
        add (time, targets, { 0xf2, static_cast<juce::uint8> (sixteenths & 0x7f), static_cast<juce::uint8> ((sixteenths >> 7) & 0x7f) });
    }

    /** MTC full frame: the time as hours, minutes, seconds and frames, at once. */
    void fullFrame (double time, juce::uint32 targets, double seconds, Rate rate) noexcept
    {
        if (targets == 0)
            return;

        const auto frame = static_cast<juce::int64> (std::floor (juce::jmax (0.0, seconds) * framesPerSecond (rate) + 1.0e-6));
        const auto tc = timecodeOf (frame, rate);

        add (time, targets, { 0xf0, 0x7f, 0x7f, 0x01, 0x01,
                              static_cast<juce::uint8> ((static_cast<int> (rate) << 5) | (tc[0] & 0x1f)),
                              static_cast<juce::uint8> (tc[1]), static_cast<juce::uint8> (tc[2]), static_cast<juce::uint8> (tc[3]),
                              0xf7 });
    }

    /** In time order, keeping the order of messages due at the same moment (Start before the first tick). */
    void sort() noexcept
    {
        for (int i = 1; i < count; ++i)
        {
            const auto message = messages[i];
            int j = i - 1;

            while (j >= 0 && messages[j].time > message.time)
            {
                messages[j + 1] = messages[j];
                --j;
            }

            messages[j + 1] = message;
        }
    }
};

namespace
{
    /** A quarter-frame message's data byte. Each group of eight (two frames) spells out the time
        at its first frame, a nibble at a time, the last one with the frame rate. */
    juce::uint8 quarterFrameData (juce::int64 quarter, MidiSync::Rate rate) noexcept
    {
        const auto piece = static_cast<int> (quarter & 7);
        const auto tc = MidiSync::Planner::timecodeOf ((quarter >> 3) * 2, rate);
        int value = 0;

        switch (piece)
        {
            case 0:  value = tc[3] & 0x0f; break;
            case 1:  value = (tc[3] >> 4) & 0x01; break;
            case 2:  value = tc[2] & 0x0f; break;
            case 3:  value = (tc[2] >> 4) & 0x03; break;
            case 4:  value = tc[1] & 0x0f; break;
            case 5:  value = (tc[1] >> 4) & 0x03; break;
            case 6:  value = tc[0] & 0x0f; break;
            default: value = ((tc[0] >> 4) & 0x01) | (static_cast<int> (rate) << 1); break;
        }

        return static_cast<juce::uint8> ((piece << 4) | value);
    }
}

//==============================================================================
double MidiSync::Planner::framesPerSecond (Rate rate) noexcept
{
    switch (rate)
    {
        case Rate::fps24:        return 24.0;
        case Rate::fps25:        return 25.0;
        case Rate::fps2997drop:  return 30000.0 / 1001.0;
        case Rate::fps30:        return 30.0;
    }

    return 30.0;
}

std::array<int, 4> MidiSync::Planner::timecodeOf (juce::int64 frame, Rate rate) noexcept
{
    const int nominal = rate == Rate::fps24 ? 24 : rate == Rate::fps25 ? 25 : 30;
    frame = juce::jmax<juce::int64> (0, frame);

    // Drop frame: the numbers 00 and 01 are skipped at the start of every minute, except every tenth.
    if (rate == Rate::fps2997drop)
    {
        constexpr juce::int64 perTenMinutes = 17982, perMinute = 1798;
        const auto tens = frame / perTenMinutes;
        const auto rest = frame % perTenMinutes;
        frame += 18 * tens + (rest > 1 ? 2 * ((rest - 2) / perMinute) : 0);
    }

    const auto seconds = frame / nominal;
    return { static_cast<int> ((seconds / 3600) % 24), static_cast<int> ((seconds / 60) % 60),
             static_cast<int> (seconds % 60), static_cast<int> (frame % nominal) };
}

void MidiSync::Planner::resync (double ppq, double seconds, Rate rate) noexcept
{
    nextTick = static_cast<juce::int64> (std::ceil (ppq * ticksPerQuarter - 1.0e-6));
    nextQuarter = static_cast<juce::int64> (std::ceil (seconds * 4.0 * framesPerSecond (rate) - 1.0e-6));
    lastRate = rate;
}

void MidiSync::Planner::reset() noexcept
{
    running = false;
    runningClock = 0;
    toldStopped = -1.0;
    toldStoppedSeconds = -1.0;
}

int MidiSync::Planner::plan (const Transport& transport, double sampleRate, double blockTime, double delayMs,
                             juce::uint32 clock, juce::uint32 startOnly, juce::uint32 timecode, Rate rate,
                             Message* messages, int maxOut) noexcept
{
    Out out { messages, maxOut };

    if (sampleRate <= 0.0)
        return 0;

    const auto msPerSample = 1000.0 / sampleRate;
    const auto timeAt = [&] (double sampleOffset) { return blockTime + delayMs + sampleOffset * msPerSample; };
    const auto segments = transport.getNumSegments();

    if (segments == 0)
    {
        if (running)
        {
            out.add (timeAt (0.0), runningClock, { 0xfc });
            reset();
        }

        // Where the song is, each time it moves while stopped: the devices follow it there.
        const auto position = transport.getBlockStart();

        const auto seconds = transport.getBlockStartSeconds();

        if (std::abs (position - toldStopped) > epsilon || std::abs (seconds - toldStoppedSeconds) > 0.5 / sampleRate)
        {
            toldStopped = position;
            toldStoppedSeconds = seconds;
            out.songPosition (timeAt (0.0), clock & ~startOnly, position);
            out.fullFrame (timeAt (0.0), timecode, transport.getBlockStartSeconds(), rate);
        }

        return out.count;
    }

    const auto perSecond = 4.0 * framesPerSecond (rate);

    for (int i = 0; i < segments; ++i)
    {
        const auto& segment = transport.getSegment (i);
        const auto at = timeAt (segment.offset);
        const auto ppqPerSample = segment.perSample;   // the tempo may ramp: each stretch has its own
        const auto previousEnd = i > 0 ? transport.getSegment (i - 1).to : lastEnd;
        const auto jumped = std::abs (segment.from - previousEnd) > 1.0e-6;

        // The song's time jumps without the position moving when the tempo before it changes.
        const auto previousEndSeconds = i > 0 ? transport.getSegment (i - 1).seconds + transport.getSegment (i - 1).length / sampleRate : lastEndSeconds;
        const auto timeJumped = std::abs (segment.seconds - previousEndSeconds) > 0.5 / sampleRate;

        if (! running)
        {
            // From the top: Start. From anywhere else: where, then Continue (unless a device takes Start only).
            const auto fromTop = segment.from < 1.0e-6;
            const auto starters = clock & (fromTop ? clock : startOnly);
            const auto continuers = clock & ~starters;

            // A device counts from the first clock after Start or Continue, and Song Position names
            // a sixteenth: the clock begins on the next sixteenth, the one Song Position names.
            const auto sixteenth = static_cast<juce::int64> (std::ceil (segment.from * 4.0 - 1.0e-6));

            out.songPosition (at, continuers, static_cast<double> (sixteenth) / 4.0);
            out.add (at, continuers, { 0xfb });
            out.add (at, starters, { 0xfa });
            out.fullFrame (at, timecode, segment.seconds, rate);

            running = true;
            runningClock = clock;
            resync (segment.from, segment.seconds, rate);
            nextTick = sixteenth * 6;
        }
        else if (jumped || timeJumped || rate != lastRate)
        {
            // The loop went round (or the frame rate changed, or a tempo before the song position
            // did): where the song is now. The clock follows the quarter notes, the timecode the time.
            if (jumped)
                out.songPosition (at, runningClock, segment.from);

            out.fullFrame (at, timecode, segment.seconds, rate);
            resync (segment.from, segment.seconds, rate);
        }

        // Clock: 24 ticks a quarter note, tick k at k/24.
        for (; static_cast<double> (nextTick) < segment.to * ticksPerQuarter - epsilon && out.count < maxOut; ++nextTick)
            out.add (timeAt (segment.offset + (static_cast<double> (nextTick) / ticksPerQuarter - segment.from) / ppqPerSample),
                     runningClock, { 0xf8 });

        // Timecode: four quarter frames a frame, on the song's own time.
        const auto secondsFrom = segment.seconds;
        const auto secondsTo = segment.seconds + segment.length / sampleRate;

        for (; static_cast<double> (nextQuarter) < secondsTo * perSecond - epsilon && out.count < maxOut; ++nextQuarter)
        {
            const auto seconds = static_cast<double> (nextQuarter) / perSecond;
            out.add (timeAt (segment.offset + (seconds - secondsFrom) * sampleRate), timecode, { 0xf1, quarterFrameData (nextQuarter, rate) });
        }
    }

    lastEnd = transport.getSegment (segments - 1).to;
    lastEndSeconds = transport.getSegment (segments - 1).seconds + transport.getSegment (segments - 1).length / sampleRate;
    out.sort();
    return out.count;
}

int MidiSync::Planner::halt (double now, Message* messages, int maxOut) noexcept
{
    Out out { messages, maxOut };

    if (running)
    {
        out.add (now, runningClock, { 0xfc });
        reset();
    }

    return out.count;
}

//==============================================================================
MidiSync::MidiSync()
    : juce::Thread ("Sonify MIDI sync")
{
    startThread (juce::Thread::Priority::highest);
}

MidiSync::~MidiSync()
{
    stopThread (2000);

    // Whatever is still queued (a Stop on the way out) goes now.
    for (;;)
    {
        int start1 = 0, size1 = 0, start2 = 0, size2 = 0;
        queue.prepareToRead (1, start1, size1, start2, size2);

        if (size1 <= 0)
            break;

        const auto message = queued[static_cast<size_t> (start1)];
        queue.finishedRead (1);
        send (message);
    }
}

MidiSync::Rate MidiSync::rateFromName (const juce::String& name) noexcept
{
    if (name == "24")     return Rate::fps24;
    if (name == "25")     return Rate::fps25;
    if (name == "29.97")  return Rate::fps2997drop;
    return Rate::fps30;
}

void MidiSync::setTargets (const std::vector<Target>& targets, Rate rate)
{
    // One output per port, whatever the devices on it ask for.
    std::vector<Target> merged;

    for (const auto& target : targets)
    {
        if (target.output.isEmpty() || ! (target.clock || target.timecode))
            continue;

        auto existing = std::find_if (merged.begin(), merged.end(), [&] (const Target& t) { return t.output == target.output; });

        if (existing == merged.end())
        {
            if (merged.size() < static_cast<size_t> (maxTargets))
                merged.push_back (target);

            continue;
        }

        existing->clock = existing->clock || target.clock;
        existing->clockStart = existing->clockStart || (target.clock && target.clockStart);
        existing->timecode = existing->timecode || target.timecode;
    }

    // Nothing more is queued for the outputs while they change.
    const auto wasClocked = clockOutputs.exchange (0);
    startOnlyOutputs.store (0);
    timecodeOutputs.store (0);

    juce::uint32 clock = 0, startOnly = 0, timecode = 0;
    const auto available = juce::MidiOutput::getAvailableDevices();

    {
        const juce::ScopedLock sl (outputLock);
        problems.clear();

        std::array<std::unique_ptr<juce::MidiOutput>, maxTargets> kept;
        std::array<juce::String, maxTargets> keptNames;
        std::array<bool, maxTargets> wasOpen {};

        for (size_t j = 0; j < outputs.size(); ++j)
            wasOpen[j] = outputs[j] != nullptr;

        const auto place = [&] (size_t j, std::unique_ptr<juce::MidiOutput> output, const Target& target)
        {
            kept[j] = std::move (output);
            keptNames[j] = target.output;

            if (target.clock)                       clock |= 1u << j;
            if (target.clock && target.clockStart)  startOnly |= 1u << j;
            if (target.timecode)                    timecode |= 1u << j;
        };

        // A port already open stays open, in its place, so what's already queued for it still
        // reaches it (and if its clock is turned off, it hears Stop).
        for (const auto& target : merged)
        {
            for (size_t j = 0; j < outputs.size(); ++j)
            {
                if (outputs[j] == nullptr || outputNames[j] != target.output)
                    continue;

                if ((wasClocked & (1u << j)) != 0 && ! target.clock)
                    outputs[j]->sendMessageNow (juce::MidiMessage::midiStop());

                place (j, std::move (outputs[j]), target);
                break;
            }
        }

        // New ports open, in places nothing was queued for.
        for (const auto& target : merged)
        {
            if (std::find (keptNames.begin(), keptNames.end(), target.output) != keptNames.end())
                continue;

            std::unique_ptr<juce::MidiOutput> output;

            for (const auto& info : available)
                if (output == nullptr && info.name == target.output)
                    output = juce::MidiOutput::openDevice (info.identifier);

            if (output == nullptr)
            {
                problems.add (target.output);
                continue;
            }

            auto slot = kept.size();

            for (size_t j = 0; j < kept.size() && slot == kept.size(); ++j)
                if (kept[j] == nullptr && ! wasOpen[j])
                    slot = j;

            for (size_t j = 0; j < kept.size() && slot == kept.size(); ++j)
                if (kept[j] == nullptr)
                    slot = j;

            if (slot < kept.size())
                place (slot, std::move (output), target);
        }

        // The ports nobody sends to any more close; one still running a clock hears Stop first.
        for (size_t j = 0; j < outputs.size(); ++j)
        {
            if (outputs[j] == nullptr)
                continue;

            if ((wasClocked & (1u << j)) != 0)
                outputs[j]->sendMessageNow (juce::MidiMessage::midiStop());

            outputs[j].reset();
        }

        for (size_t j = 0; j < outputs.size(); ++j)
        {
            outputs[j] = std::move (kept[j]);
            outputNames[j] = keptNames[j];
        }
    }

    // The audio thread starts afresh: devices playing hear where the song is, and Continue.
    restart.store (true);
    rateSetting.store (static_cast<int> (rate));
    startOnlyOutputs.store (startOnly);
    timecodeOutputs.store (timecode);
    clockOutputs.store (clock);
}

juce::StringArray MidiSync::getProblems() const
{
    const juce::ScopedLock sl (outputLock);
    return problems;
}

void MidiSync::process (const Transport& transport, double sampleRate, double blockTime, double delayMs) noexcept
{
    if (restart.exchange (false))
        planner.reset();

    const auto clock = clockOutputs.load (std::memory_order_relaxed);
    const auto timecode = timecodeOutputs.load (std::memory_order_relaxed);

    if ((clock | timecode) == 0)
        return;

    const auto count = planner.plan (transport, sampleRate, blockTime, delayMs, clock,
                                     startOnlyOutputs.load (std::memory_order_relaxed), timecode,
                                     static_cast<Rate> (rateSetting.load (std::memory_order_relaxed)),
                                     scratch.data(), static_cast<int> (scratch.size()));
    queueMessages (scratch.data(), count);
}

void MidiSync::halt (double now) noexcept
{
    const auto count = planner.halt (now, scratch.data(), static_cast<int> (scratch.size()));
    queueMessages (scratch.data(), count);
}

void MidiSync::queueMessages (Message* messages, int count) noexcept
{
    for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i)
    {
        // A full queue drops the message rather than wait: the audio thread never blocks.
        const auto write = queue.write (1);

        if (write.blockSize1 > 0)
            queued[static_cast<size_t> (write.startIndex1)] = messages[i];
    }
}

void MidiSync::send (const Message& message)
{
    if (message.size <= 0)
        return;

    const juce::MidiMessage midi (message.bytes.data(), message.size);
    const juce::ScopedLock sl (outputLock);

    for (size_t i = 0; i < outputs.size(); ++i)
        if ((message.targets & (1u << i)) != 0 && outputs[i] != nullptr)
            outputs[i]->sendMessageNow (midi);
}

void MidiSync::run()
{
    while (! threadShouldExit())
    {
        int start1 = 0, size1 = 0, start2 = 0, size2 = 0;
        queue.prepareToRead (1, start1, size1, start2, size2);

        if (size1 <= 0)
        {
            wait (1);
            continue;
        }

        const auto message = queued[static_cast<size_t> (start1)];
        const auto ahead = message.time - juce::Time::getMillisecondCounterHiRes();

        // Asleep most of the way, awake for the last moment, then out exactly on time.
        if (ahead > 1.5)
        {
            wait (juce::jlimit (1, 10, static_cast<int> (ahead - 1.0)));
            continue;
        }

        if (ahead > 0.05)
        {
            juce::Thread::yield();
            continue;
        }

        queue.finishedRead (1);
        send (message);
    }
}

// D:\workspace\Fanan_web_hub\src\MidiSync.h

#pragma once

#include <juce_audio_devices/juce_audio_devices.h>

#include "Transport.h"

#include <array>
#include <atomic>
#include <memory>
#include <vector>

//==============================================================================
/**
    MIDI clock and MIDI timecode for external devices, as Studio One sends them (Settings >
    External Devices: Send MIDI Clock, Use MIDI Clock Start, Send MIDI Timecode). Sonify is
    the master: drum machines, arpeggiators and sequencers follow its tempo and position.

    Clock: 24 ticks a quarter note while Sonify plays. Playing from the top of the song sends
    Start; from anywhere else, where (Song Position Pointer) and then Continue, except to a
    device that takes Start only ("Use MIDI Clock Start"). Stopping sends Stop. A jump while
    playing (the loop going round) and a new position while stopped send Song Position.

    Timecode (MTC): quarter-frame messages while Sonify plays, and a full-frame message wherever
    playing starts, jumps, or the song position is moved. The song's start is 00:00:00:00.

    The audio thread works out, block by block, what's due and when it's heard (the block's
    time plus the device's output latency), and queues it. A thread of its own sends each
    message at its time, so the audio thread never waits for a MIDI port or allocates.
*/
class MidiSync final : private juce::Thread
{
public:
    /** MTC frame rates, numbered as the timecode messages number them. */
    enum class Rate { fps24 = 0, fps25 = 1, fps2997drop = 2, fps30 = 3 };

    struct Target
    {
        juce::String output;            // a MIDI output port, by name
        bool clock = false;             // MIDI clock
        bool clockStart = false;        // Start only, never Song Position + Continue
        bool timecode = false;          // MIDI timecode
    };

    /** One MIDI message, queued with the time it's sent at. */
    struct Message
    {
        double time = 0.0;              // Time::getMillisecondCounterHiRes()
        juce::uint32 targets = 0;       // which outputs, one bit each
        int size = 0;
        std::array<juce::uint8, 10> bytes {};
    };

    static constexpr int maxTargets = 16;

    //==============================================================================
    /** What each block sends: the audio thread's half, on its own so it can be tested. */
    class Planner
    {
    public:
        /** This block's messages, in time order, into out (at most maxOut); returns how many.
            clock: the outputs that get clock; startOnly: those of them that take Start only;
            timecode: the outputs that get MTC. blockTime: when the block began
            (Time::getMillisecondCounterHiRes()); delayMs: until it's heard. */
        int plan (const Transport& transport, double sampleRate, double blockTime, double delayMs,
                  juce::uint32 clock, juce::uint32 startOnly, juce::uint32 timecode, Rate rate,
                  Message* out, int maxOut) noexcept;

        /** Stop, for the clock outputs that are running. */
        int halt (double now, Message* out, int maxOut) noexcept;

        /** Forgets what the devices were told: the next block starts them afresh. */
        void reset() noexcept;

        static double framesPerSecond (Rate rate) noexcept;

        /** A frame count as hours, minutes, seconds and frames (drop-frame numbering at 29.97). */
        static std::array<int, 4> timecodeOf (juce::int64 frame, Rate rate) noexcept;

    private:
        struct Out;

        bool running = false;           // the clock outputs have been started
        juce::uint32 runningClock = 0;  // the ones that were
        double lastEnd = 0.0;           // where the last block played up to, quarter notes
        double lastEndSeconds = 0.0;    // and in the song's time
        double toldStopped = -1.0;      // the position last told while stopped (-1: none yet)
        double toldStoppedSeconds = -1.0;   // and its time (a tempo changed before it moves it)
        juce::int64 nextTick = 0;       // the next clock tick: tick k is at k/24 quarter notes
        juce::int64 nextQuarter = 0;    // the next MTC quarter frame: q is at q / (4 fps) seconds
        Rate lastRate = Rate::fps30;

        /** Counting again from here (quarter notes, and the song's time in seconds). */
        void resync (double ppq, double seconds, Rate rate) noexcept;
    };

    //==============================================================================
    MidiSync();
    ~MidiSync() override;

    /** Message thread: who gets what, and the timecode's frame rate. Opens and closes the MIDI
        outputs as needed (outputs no device sends to stay closed, for other apps to use). */
    void setTargets (const std::vector<Target>& targets, Rate rate);

    /** The outputs that couldn't be opened (another app may hold them). Message thread. */
    juce::StringArray getProblems() const;

    /** Audio thread, once per device block, after the transport has planned it. */
    void process (const Transport& transport, double sampleRate, double blockTime, double delayMs) noexcept;

    /** The device stops playing the song (a mixdown takes over, the device stops): devices
        running are told to stop. Audio thread, or once the device has stopped. */
    void halt (double now) noexcept;

    static Rate rateFromName (const juce::String& name) noexcept;

private:
    void run() override;
    void queueMessages (Message* messages, int count) noexcept;
    void send (const Message& message);

    Planner planner;                                // audio thread
    std::array<Message, 512> scratch {};            // audio thread: this block's messages

    static constexpr int queueSize = 4096;
    juce::AbstractFifo queue { queueSize };         // audio thread writes, the sender reads
    std::array<Message, queueSize> queued {};

    std::atomic<juce::uint32> clockOutputs { 0 }, startOnlyOutputs { 0 }, timecodeOutputs { 0 };
    std::atomic<int> rateSetting { static_cast<int> (Rate::fps30) };
    std::atomic<bool> restart { false };            // the outputs changed: the planner starts afresh

    juce::CriticalSection outputLock;               // the sender and the message thread
    std::array<std::unique_ptr<juce::MidiOutput>, maxTargets> outputs;
    std::array<juce::String, maxTargets> outputNames;
    juce::StringArray problems;

    JUCE_DECLARE_NON_COPYABLE_WITH_LEAK_DETECTOR (MidiSync)
};

#include "Mp3Encoder.h"

#include <cmath>

//==============================================================================
// LAME's C functions, looked up in the library (lame.h's names and signatures).
struct Mp3Encoder::Lame
{
#if JUCE_WINDOWS
   #define FANAN_LAME_CALL __cdecl
#else
   #define FANAN_LAME_CALL
#endif

    using Init           = void* (FANAN_LAME_CALL*) ();
    using SetInt         = int   (FANAN_LAME_CALL*) (void*, int);
    using InitParams     = int   (FANAN_LAME_CALL*) (void*);
    using EncodeFloat    = int   (FANAN_LAME_CALL*) (void*, const float*, const float*, int, unsigned char*, int);
    using Flush          = int   (FANAN_LAME_CALL*) (void*, unsigned char*, int);
    using LameTag        = size_t (FANAN_LAME_CALL*) (const void*, unsigned char*, size_t);
    using Close          = int   (FANAN_LAME_CALL*) (void*);

    Lame()
    {
        const auto folder = juce::File::getSpecialLocation (juce::File::currentExecutableFile).getParentDirectory();

       #if JUCE_WINDOWS
        const auto file = folder.getChildFile ("mp3lame.dll");
       #elif JUCE_MAC
        const auto file = folder.getChildFile ("libmp3lame.dylib");
       #else
        const auto file = folder.getChildFile ("libmp3lame.so");
       #endif

        // A library named elsewhere (tests).
        auto path = juce::SystemStats::getEnvironmentVariable ("SONIFY_MP3LAME", {});

        if (path.isEmpty())
        {
            if (! file.existsAsFile())
            {
                problem = "MP3 export needs LAME (" + file.getFileName() + ") next to Sonify: building Sonify puts it there.";
                return;
            }

            path = file.getFullPathName();
        }

        if (! library.open (path))
        {
            problem = "LAME (" + juce::File (path).getFileName() + ") couldn't be loaded.";
            return;
        }

        const auto find = [this] (const char* name) { return library.getFunction (name); };

        init          = reinterpret_cast<Init>        (find ("lame_init"));
        setInRate     = reinterpret_cast<SetInt>      (find ("lame_set_in_samplerate"));
        setChannels   = reinterpret_cast<SetInt>      (find ("lame_set_num_channels"));
        setBitRate    = reinterpret_cast<SetInt>      (find ("lame_set_brate"));
        setMode       = reinterpret_cast<SetInt>      (find ("lame_set_mode"));
        setQuality    = reinterpret_cast<SetInt>      (find ("lame_set_quality"));
        setVbr        = reinterpret_cast<SetInt>      (find ("lame_set_VBR"));
        setVbrTag     = reinterpret_cast<SetInt>      (find ("lame_set_bWriteVbrTag"));
        initParams    = reinterpret_cast<InitParams>  (find ("lame_init_params"));
        encode        = reinterpret_cast<EncodeFloat> (find ("lame_encode_buffer_ieee_float"));
        flush         = reinterpret_cast<Flush>       (find ("lame_encode_flush"));
        lameTag       = reinterpret_cast<LameTag>     (find ("lame_get_lametag_frame"));
        close         = reinterpret_cast<Close>       (find ("lame_close"));

        if (init == nullptr || setInRate == nullptr || setChannels == nullptr || setBitRate == nullptr || setMode == nullptr
            || setQuality == nullptr || setVbr == nullptr || setVbrTag == nullptr || initParams == nullptr || encode == nullptr
            || flush == nullptr || lameTag == nullptr || close == nullptr)
            problem = "This LAME (" + juce::File (path).getFileName() + ") is missing what Sonify needs.";
    }

    juce::DynamicLibrary library;
    juce::String problem;

    Init init = nullptr;
    SetInt setInRate = nullptr, setChannels = nullptr, setBitRate = nullptr, setMode = nullptr, setQuality = nullptr,
           setVbr = nullptr, setVbrTag = nullptr;
    InitParams initParams = nullptr;
    EncodeFloat encode = nullptr;
    Flush flush = nullptr;
    LameTag lameTag = nullptr;
    Close close = nullptr;

   #undef FANAN_LAME_CALL
};

Mp3Encoder::Lame& Mp3Encoder::lame()
{
    static Lame instance;
    return instance;
}

juce::String Mp3Encoder::problem()
{
    return lame().problem;
}

//==============================================================================
Mp3Encoder::Mp3Encoder() = default;

Mp3Encoder::~Mp3Encoder()
{
    if (flags != nullptr)
        lame().close (flags);

    // Never finished: no half file left behind.
    if (stream != nullptr)
    {
        stream.reset();
        target.deleteFile();
    }
}

juce::Result Mp3Encoder::open (const juce::File& file, double sampleRate, int kbps)
{
    auto& api = lame();

    if (api.problem.isNotEmpty())
        return juce::Result::fail (api.problem);

    if (flags != nullptr)
        return juce::Result::fail ("This MP3 has already started.");

    flags = api.init();

    if (flags == nullptr)
        return juce::Result::fail ("LAME couldn't start.");

    // The bit rates MP3 has, nearest to the one asked for.
    static constexpr int rates[] = { 32, 40, 48, 56, 64, 80, 96, 112, 128, 160, 192, 224, 256, 320 };
    int rate = 320;

    for (const auto r : rates)
        if (std::abs (r - kbps) < std::abs (rate - kbps))
            rate = r;

    api.setInRate (flags, juce::roundToInt (sampleRate));
    api.setChannels (flags, 2);
    api.setBitRate (flags, rate);
    api.setMode (flags, 1);         // joint stereo
    api.setQuality (flags, 2);      // LAME's "high quality" (0 best .. 9 fastest)
    api.setVbr (flags, 0);          // constant bit rate
    api.setVbrTag (flags, 1);       // the LAME tag: exact length for players

    if (api.initParams (flags) < 0)
        return juce::Result::fail ("LAME can't write " + juce::String (juce::roundToInt (sampleRate)) + " Hz at " + juce::String (rate) + " kbps.");

    file.deleteFile();
    stream = std::make_unique<juce::FileOutputStream> (file);

    if (! stream->openedOk())
    {
        stream.reset();
        return juce::Result::fail ("Couldn't write " + file.getFullPathName());
    }

    target = file;
    failed = false;
    return juce::Result::ok();
}

bool Mp3Encoder::write (const float* left, const float* right, int numSamples)
{
    if (flags == nullptr || stream == nullptr || failed || numSamples <= 0)
        return ! failed;

    // As LAME asks: room for 1.25 times the samples plus 7200 bytes.
    const auto needed = static_cast<size_t> (numSamples + numSamples / 4 + 7200);

    if (buffer.size() < needed)
        buffer.resize (needed);

    const auto written = lame().encode (flags, left, right, numSamples, buffer.data(), static_cast<int> (buffer.size()));

    if (written < 0 || (written > 0 && ! stream->write (buffer.data(), static_cast<size_t> (written))))
        failed = true;

    return ! failed;
}

juce::Result Mp3Encoder::close()
{
    if (flags == nullptr || stream == nullptr)
        return juce::Result::fail ("This MP3 never started.");

    auto& api = lame();

    if (buffer.size() < 7200)
        buffer.resize (7200);

    const auto last = api.flush (flags, buffer.data(), static_cast<int> (buffer.size()));

    if (last < 0 || (last > 0 && ! stream->write (buffer.data(), static_cast<size_t> (last))))
        failed = true;

    // The LAME tag goes over the first frame, which LAME kept for it.
    if (! failed)
    {
        std::vector<unsigned char> tag (2880);
        const auto size = api.lameTag (flags, tag.data(), tag.size());

        if (size > 0 && size <= tag.size())
        {
            stream->flush();
            failed = ! stream->setPosition (0) || ! stream->write (tag.data(), size);
        }
    }

    stream->flush();
    failed = failed || stream->getStatus().failed();

    api.close (flags);
    flags = nullptr;
    stream.reset();

    if (failed)
    {
        target.deleteFile();
        return juce::Result::fail ("Couldn't write " + target.getFullPathName());
    }

    return juce::Result::ok();
}

#pragma once

#include <juce_core/juce_core.h>

#include <memory>
#include <vector>

//==============================================================================
/**
    Writes an MP3 file with LAME (mp3lame.dll next to Sonify, which the build puts there; loaded
    the first time it's needed). Constant bit rate, joint stereo, LAME's high-quality setting;
    the LAME tag at the start of the file carries the exact length, so players don't add silence.

    LAME takes any input rate and writes the nearest one MP3 has (at most 48 kHz).
*/
class Mp3Encoder final
{
public:
    Mp3Encoder();
    ~Mp3Encoder();

    /** "" when LAME is there and loads; otherwise why not. */
    static juce::String problem();

    /** Starts the file (replacing one already there). kbps: 32 to 320. */
    juce::Result open (const juce::File& file, double sampleRate, int kbps);

    /** Samples in -1..1, both channels the same length. */
    bool write (const float* left, const float* right, int numSamples);

    /** Ends the file: what LAME still holds, then its tag. */
    juce::Result close();

private:
    struct Lame;
    static Lame& lame();

    void* flags = nullptr;
    std::unique_ptr<juce::FileOutputStream> stream;
    std::vector<unsigned char> buffer;
    juce::File target;
    bool failed = false;

    JUCE_DECLARE_NON_COPYABLE_WITH_LEAK_DETECTOR (Mp3Encoder)
};
