// D:\workspace\Fanan_web_hub\src\SfzLoops.cpp

#include "SfzLoops.h"
#include "SfzFile.h"

#include <juce_audio_formats/juce_audio_formats.h>

#include <algorithm>
#include <cmath>
#include <limits>
#include <map>

namespace
{
    using Text = std::u32string;

    Text toText (const juce::String& s)
    {
        Text t;
        t.reserve (static_cast<size_t> (s.length()));

        for (auto p = s.getCharPointer(); ! p.isEmpty();)
            t.push_back (static_cast<char32_t> (p.getAndAdvance()));

        return t;
    }

    juce::String fromText (const Text& t, size_t start, size_t end)
    {
        juce::String s;
        s.preallocateBytes (end - start + 1);

        for (auto i = start; i < end && i < t.size(); ++i)
            s += static_cast<juce::juce_wchar> (t[i]);

        return s;
    }

    juce::String fromText (const Text& t)
    {
        return fromText (t, 0, t.size());
    }

    bool isSpace (char32_t c) noexcept    { return c == ' ' || c == '\t' || c == '\n' || c == '\r'; }

    bool isNameChar (char32_t c) noexcept
    {
        return (c >= 'a' && c <= 'z') || (c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z') || (c >= '0' && c <= '9') || c == '_' || c == '$';
    }

    /** The text with its comments (// to the line's end, and block comments) made spaces. */
    Text masked (const Text& t)
    {
        auto m = t;

        for (size_t i = 0; i + 1 < m.size(); ++i)
        {
            if (m[i] == '/' && m[i + 1] == '/')
            {
                while (i < m.size() && m[i] != '\n')
                    m[i++] = ' ';
            }
            else if (m[i] == '/' && m[i + 1] == '*')
            {
                while (i < m.size() && ! (m[i] == '*' && i + 1 < m.size() && m[i + 1] == '/'))
                {
                    if (m[i] != '\n')
                        m[i] = ' ';

                    ++i;
                }

                if (i + 1 < m.size())
                {
                    m[i] = ' ';
                    m[i + 1] = ' ';
                    ++i;
                }
            }
        }

        return m;
    }

    /** Opcodes whose values may hold spaces: they run to the line's end (or the next opcode). */
    bool isPathOpcode (const juce::String& name)
    {
        return name == "sample" || name == "default_path" || name.startsWith ("label") || name.endsWith ("_label") || name == "image";
    }

    /** A key as the SFZ may write it: a number, or a note name (c4 is 60, c#4 and db4 61). */
    int keyValue (const juce::String& value, int fallback)
    {
        const auto v = value.trim().toLowerCase();

        if (v.isEmpty())
            return fallback;

        if (v[0] == '-' || juce::CharacterFunctions::isDigit (v[0]))
            return juce::jlimit (0, 127, v.getIntValue());

        static const int semitones[] { 9, 11, 0, 2, 4, 5, 7 };   // a b c d e f g

        if (v[0] < 'a' || v[0] > 'g')
            return fallback;

        auto note = semitones[v[0] - 'a'];
        int at = 1;

        if (at < v.length() && v[at] == '#')
        {
            ++note;
            ++at;
        }
        else if (at < v.length() && v[at] == 'b' && at + 1 < v.length() && (v[at + 1] == '-' || juce::CharacterFunctions::isDigit (v[at + 1])))
        {
            --note;
            ++at;
        }

        const auto octave = v.substring (at).getIntValue();
        return juce::jlimit (0, 127, (octave + 1) * 12 + note);
    }

    juce::File resolve (const juce::File& folder, const juce::String& path)
    {
        auto native = path.trim().replaceCharacter ('\\', '/');

        if (native.isEmpty())
            return folder;

        if (juce::File::isAbsolutePath (native.replaceCharacter ('/', juce::File::getSeparatorChar())))
            return juce::File (native.replaceCharacter ('/', juce::File::getSeparatorChar()));

        auto file = folder;

        for (const auto& part : juce::StringArray::fromTokens (native, "/", ""))
        {
            if (part.isEmpty() || part == ".")
                continue;

            file = part == ".." ? file.getParentDirectory() : file.getChildFile (part);
        }

        return file;
    }

    bool isLoopMode (const juce::String& mode)
    {
        return mode == "loop_sustain" || mode == "loop_continuous";
    }

    bool isLoopOpcode (const juce::String& name)
    {
        return name == "loop_mode" || name == "loopmode" || name == "loop_start" || name == "loopstart"
            || name == "loop_end" || name == "loopend" || name == "loop_crossfade";
    }

    double fileRate (const juce::File& file)
    {
        juce::AudioFormatManager formats;
        formats.registerBasicFormats();
        std::unique_ptr<juce::AudioFormatReader> reader (formats.createReaderFor (file));
        return reader != nullptr ? reader->sampleRate : 44100.0;
    }

    juce::String number (double value, int decimals)
    {
        return juce::String (value, decimals);
    }
}

//==============================================================================
bool SfzLoops::load (const juce::File& sfz, Patch& patch, juce::String& why)
{
    patch = {};

    if (! sfz.existsAsFile())
    {
        why = "File not found: " + sfz.getFileName();
        return false;
    }

    const auto raw = sfz.loadFileAsString();
    patch.file = sfz;
    patch.crlf = raw.contains ("\r\n");
    patch.text = raw.replace ("\r\n", "\n").replace ("\r", "\n");

    const auto t = toText (patch.text);
    const auto m = masked (t);
    const auto n = m.size();
    const auto sfzFolder = sfz.getParentDirectory();
    auto defaultFolder = sfzFolder;

    enum class Section { none, control, global, master, group, region, other };
    auto section = Section::none;
    std::map<juce::String, juce::String> global, master, group, own;
    bool inRegion = false;
    Region region;

    const auto close = [&] (size_t at)
    {
        if (! inRegion)
            return;

        inRegion = false;
        region.bodyEnd = static_cast<int> (at);

        auto ops = global;

        for (const auto& [k, v] : master) ops[k] = v;
        for (const auto& [k, v] : group)  ops[k] = v;

        const auto inheritedMode = ops.count ("loop_mode") != 0 ? ops["loop_mode"] : (ops.count ("loopmode") != 0 ? ops["loopmode"] : juce::String());
        region.inheritedLoop = isLoopMode (inheritedMode.trim().toLowerCase());

        for (const auto& [k, v] : own) ops[k] = v;

        region.sample = ops["sample"].trim();

        if (region.sample.isEmpty() || region.sample.startsWithChar ('*'))
            return;   // a generator (*sine...), or nothing to play

        region.file = resolve (defaultFolder, region.sample);

        if (ops.count ("key") != 0)
            region.lokey = region.hikey = region.keycenter = keyValue (ops["key"], 60);

        if (ops.count ("lokey") != 0)            region.lokey = keyValue (ops["lokey"], region.lokey);
        if (ops.count ("hikey") != 0)            region.hikey = keyValue (ops["hikey"], region.hikey);
        if (ops.count ("pitch_keycenter") != 0)  region.keycenter = keyValue (ops["pitch_keycenter"], region.keycenter);
        if (ops.count ("lovel") != 0)            region.lovel = juce::jlimit (0, 127, ops["lovel"].getIntValue());
        if (ops.count ("hivel") != 0)            region.hivel = juce::jlimit (0, 127, ops["hivel"].getIntValue());

        const auto pick = [&ops] (const char* a, const char* b) -> juce::String
        {
            if (ops.count (a) != 0) return ops[a];
            if (ops.count (b) != 0) return ops[b];
            return {};
        };

        region.loopMode = pick ("loop_mode", "loopmode").trim().toLowerCase();
        region.loopStart = juce::jmax<juce::int64> (0, pick ("loop_start", "loopstart").getLargeIntValue());
        region.loopEnd = juce::jmax<juce::int64> (0, pick ("loop_end", "loopend").getLargeIntValue());
        region.looped = region.loopEnd > region.loopStart && (isLoopMode (region.loopMode) || region.loopMode.isEmpty());

        if (ops.count ("loop_crossfade") != 0)
        {
            const auto rate = fileRate (region.file);
            region.crossfade = static_cast<int> (std::lround (Sfz::readCrossfade (ops["loop_crossfade"], rate) * rate));
        }

        patch.regions.push_back (region);
    };

    for (size_t i = 0; i < n;)
    {
        const auto c = m[i];

        if (isSpace (c))
        {
            ++i;
            continue;
        }

        if (c == '<')
        {
            auto j = i + 1;

            while (j < n && m[j] != '>' && m[j] != '\n')
                ++j;

            if (j >= n || m[j] != '>')
            {
                ++i;
                continue;
            }

            const auto name = fromText (t, i + 1, j).trim().toLowerCase();
            close (i);
            own.clear();

            if (name == "region")
            {
                section = Section::region;
                inRegion = true;
                region = {};
                region.headerStart = static_cast<int> (i);
                region.bodyStart = static_cast<int> (j + 1);
            }
            else if (name == "group")    { section = Section::group;  group.clear(); }
            else if (name == "master")   { section = Section::master; master.clear(); group.clear(); }
            else if (name == "global")   { section = Section::global; global.clear(); master.clear(); group.clear(); }
            else if (name == "control")  { section = Section::control; }
            else                         { section = Section::other; }

            i = j + 1;
            continue;
        }

        if (c == '#')
        {
            while (i < n && m[i] != '\n')
                ++i;

            continue;
        }

        const auto nameStart = i;

        while (i < n && isNameChar (m[i]))
            ++i;

        if (i == nameStart || i >= n || m[i] != '=')
        {
            while (i < n && ! isSpace (m[i]) && m[i] != '<')
                ++i;

            if (i == nameStart)
                ++i;

            continue;
        }

        const auto name = fromText (t, nameStart, i).toLowerCase();
        const auto valueStart = ++i;
        auto end = i;

        if (isPathOpcode (name))
        {
            // To the line's end, or before the next opcode on it.
            while (end < n && m[end] != '\n' && m[end] != '<')
            {
                if (isSpace (m[end]))
                {
                    auto k = end;

                    while (k < n && (m[k] == ' ' || m[k] == '\t'))
                        ++k;

                    auto q = k;

                    while (q < n && isNameChar (m[q]))
                        ++q;

                    if (q > k && q < n && m[q] == '=')
                        break;
                }

                ++end;
            }

            while (end > valueStart && isSpace (m[end - 1]))
                --end;
        }
        else
        {
            while (end < n && ! isSpace (m[end]) && m[end] != '<')
                ++end;
        }

        const auto value = fromText (t, valueStart, end);

        switch (section)
        {
            case Section::region:  own[name] = value; region.own.push_back ({ name, static_cast<int> (nameStart), static_cast<int> (valueStart), static_cast<int> (end) }); break;
            case Section::group:   group[name] = value; break;
            case Section::master:  master[name] = value; break;
            case Section::global:  global[name] = value; break;
            case Section::control:
            case Section::none:
            case Section::other:
            default:               break;
        }

        if (name == "default_path" && section == Section::control)
        {
            defaultFolder = resolve (sfzFolder, value);
            patch.paths.push_back ({ static_cast<int> (valueStart), static_cast<int> (end), defaultFolder, true, value.containsChar ('\\') });
        }
        else if (name == "sample" && ! value.trim().startsWithChar ('*'))
        {
            patch.paths.push_back ({ static_cast<int> (valueStart), static_cast<int> (end), resolve (defaultFolder, value), false, value.containsChar ('\\') });
        }

        i = juce::jmax (end, valueStart);
    }

    close (n);

    if (patch.regions.empty())
    {
        why = "No regions found in " + sfz.getFileName();
        return false;
    }

    return true;
}

//==============================================================================
juce::String SfzLoops::textFor (const Patch& patch, const juce::File& target)
{
    struct Edit
    {
        int start = 0, end = 0;
        juce::String with;
    };

    std::vector<Edit> edits;
    const auto t = toText (patch.text);
    const auto m = masked (t);

    // The changed regions: their own loop opcodes out (a line left empty goes too), the loop as
    // set in after their last opcode.
    for (const auto& region : patch.regions)
    {
        if (! region.changed)
            continue;

        int insertAt = region.bodyStart;

        for (const auto& op : region.own)
        {
            if (isLoopOpcode (op.name))
            {
                auto start = op.start, end = op.end;

                // The spaces before it on its line, and the line itself when nothing else is on it
                // (a comment after it stays).
                while (start > 0 && (t[static_cast<size_t> (start - 1)] == ' ' || t[static_cast<size_t> (start - 1)] == '\t'))
                    --start;

                auto after = end;

                while (after < static_cast<int> (t.size()) && (t[static_cast<size_t> (after)] == ' ' || t[static_cast<size_t> (after)] == '\t'))
                    ++after;

                const bool lineStarts = start == 0 || t[static_cast<size_t> (start - 1)] == '\n';
                const bool lineEnds = after >= static_cast<int> (t.size()) || t[static_cast<size_t> (after)] == '\n';

                if (lineStarts && lineEnds && after < static_cast<int> (m.size()))
                    end = after + 1;
                else if (lineStarts)
                    end = after;

                edits.push_back ({ start, end, {} });
            }
            else
            {
                insertAt = juce::jmax (insertAt, op.end);
            }
        }

        juce::String loop;

        if (region.looped && region.loopEnd > region.loopStart)
        {
            const auto mode = isLoopMode (region.loopMode) ? region.loopMode : juce::String ("loop_sustain");
            loop << "\nloop_mode=" << mode << "\nloop_start=" << juce::String (region.loopStart) << "\nloop_end=" << juce::String (region.loopEnd);

            if (region.crossfade > 0)
            {
                const auto rate = fileRate (region.file);
                auto seconds = number (region.crossfade / juce::jmax (1.0, rate), 3);

                while (seconds.endsWithChar ('0'))
                    seconds = seconds.dropLastCharacters (1);

                if (seconds.endsWithChar ('.'))
                    seconds = seconds.dropLastCharacters (1);

                loop << "\nloop_crossfade=" << seconds;
            }
        }
        else if (region.inheritedLoop)
        {
            loop << "\nloop_mode=no_loop";
        }

        if (loop.isNotEmpty())
            edits.push_back ({ insertAt, insertAt, loop });
    }

    // Saved into another folder: the paths made relative to it (default_path, when there's one,
    // else each sample's).
    const auto from = patch.file.getParentDirectory();
    const auto to = target.getParentDirectory();

    if (from != to)
    {
        const bool hasDefault = std::any_of (patch.paths.begin(), patch.paths.end(), [] (const Patch::PathOpcode& p) { return p.isDefaultPath; });

        for (const auto& path : patch.paths)
        {
            if (hasDefault != path.isDefaultPath)
                continue;

            const auto original = fromText (t, static_cast<size_t> (path.valueStart), static_cast<size_t> (path.end));

            if (juce::File::isAbsolutePath (original.trim().replaceCharacter ('\\', juce::File::getSeparatorChar()).replaceCharacter ('/', juce::File::getSeparatorChar())))
                continue;

            auto relative = path.points.getRelativePathFrom (to).replaceCharacter ('\\', '/');

            if (path.isDefaultPath && relative.isNotEmpty() && ! relative.endsWithChar ('/'))
                relative << "/";

            if (path.backslash)
                relative = relative.replaceCharacter ('/', '\\');

            edits.push_back ({ path.valueStart, path.end, relative });
        }
    }

    std::sort (edits.begin(), edits.end(), [] (const Edit& a, const Edit& b) { return a.start != b.start ? a.start > b.start : a.end > b.end; });

    auto out = t;
    int lastStart = std::numeric_limits<int>::max();

    for (const auto& edit : edits)
    {
        if (edit.end > lastStart)
            continue;   // overlaps one already made

        out.replace (static_cast<size_t> (edit.start), static_cast<size_t> (edit.end - edit.start), toText (edit.with));
        lastStart = edit.start;
    }

    return fromText (out);
}

juce::Result SfzLoops::save (Patch& patch, const juce::File& target)
{
    if (patch.regions.empty())
        return juce::Result::fail ("Load an SFZ first.");

    const auto text = textFor (patch, target);

    target.getParentDirectory().createDirectory();

    if (! target.replaceWithText (text, false, false, patch.crlf ? "\r\n" : "\n"))
        return juce::Result::fail ("Sonify couldn't write " + target.getFullPathName() + ".");

    // The loops into the samples (a WAV only; other formats keep theirs in the SFZ alone).
    juce::StringArray notWritten;

    for (const auto& region : patch.regions)
    {
        if (! region.file.existsAsFile() || ! region.file.hasFileExtension ("wav"))
            continue;

        if (region.looped && region.loopEnd > region.loopStart)
        {
            if (! Sfz::setWavLoop (region.file, region.keycenter, region.loopStart, region.loopEnd))
                notWritten.addIfNotAlreadyThere (region.file.getFileName());
        }
        else if (region.changed)
        {
            if (! Sfz::setWavLoop (region.file, region.keycenter, -1, -1))
                notWritten.addIfNotAlreadyThere (region.file.getFileName());
        }
    }

    juce::String why;
    const auto keep = patch;

    if (! load (target, patch, why))
    {
        patch = keep;
        return juce::Result::fail (why);
    }

    if (! notWritten.isEmpty())
        return juce::Result::fail ("Saved " + target.getFileName() + ", but the loop couldn't be put in "
                                   + notWritten.joinIntoString (", ") + " (in use by another app?).");

    return juce::Result::ok();
}

//==============================================================================
juce::var SfzLoops::peaks (const juce::AudioBuffer<float>& audio, double sampleRate, int buckets)
{
    auto* o = new juce::DynamicObject();
    const auto frames = audio.getNumSamples();
    const auto channels = juce::jlimit (0, 2, audio.getNumChannels());
    buckets = juce::jlimit (1, 8000, juce::jmin (buckets, juce::jmax (1, frames)));

    o->setProperty ("channels", channels);
    o->setProperty ("frames", frames);
    o->setProperty ("rate", sampleRate);

    juce::Array<juce::var> all;

    for (int channel = 0; channel < channels; ++channel)
    {
        juce::Array<juce::var> list;
        list.ensureStorageAllocated (buckets * 2);
        const auto* data = audio.getReadPointer (channel);

        for (int b = 0; b < buckets; ++b)
        {
            const auto start = static_cast<int> (static_cast<juce::int64> (frames) * b / buckets);
            const auto end = juce::jmax (start + 1, static_cast<int> (static_cast<juce::int64> (frames) * (b + 1) / buckets));
            const auto range = juce::FloatVectorOperations::findMinAndMax (data + start, juce::jmin (end, frames) - start);
            list.add (juce::jlimit (-127, 127, juce::roundToInt (range.getStart() * 127.0f)));
            list.add (juce::jlimit (-127, 127, juce::roundToInt (range.getEnd() * 127.0f)));
        }

        all.add (list);
    }

    o->setProperty ("peaks", all);
    return juce::var (o);
}

double SfzLoops::keyHz (int note)
{
    return 440.0 * std::pow (2.0, (note - 69) / 12.0);
}

//==============================================================================
juce::String SfzLoops::aiGuide()
{
    return
        "You are Fanan AI inside Sonify's Sampling Studio, in its Loop Editor. You choose sustain loop points for "
        "sampled instrument notes: while a key is held, the sampler plays the attack, then repeats the loop until the "
        "key is let go. A good loop is one the listener can't hear: no click, no thump, no pitch jump, no level pump, "
        "no tone change at the seam, and long enough not to sound like a buzzing cycle.\n\n"
        "For each sample you get what it is (its key, its expected pitch, its length, the detected pitch) and a list "
        "of candidate loops found by Sonify's loop finder (each starts and ends on a rising zero crossing and is a "
        "whole number of pitch periods long), with these numbers:\n"
        "- score: the finder's own 0..1 rating (the two ends' waveform likeness, level, value and slope matches, how late it sits).\n"
        "- correlation: how alike the waveform is at the two ends over four periods (-1..1; above 0.95 is good, above 0.98 very good).\n"
        "- levelMatch: the quieter end's level over the louder's (1 = equal; under 0.85 the level will pump each cycle).\n"
        "- valueMatch, slopeMatch: how well the sample value and slope meet at the seam (1 = perfect; under 0.9 risks a click).\n"
        "- seconds, periods: the loop's length (very short loops, under about 0.1 s or 20 periods, can sound static or buzzy; "
        "longer loops keep the natural movement of chorus, vibrato, bowing or breath, but need the sound steady across them).\n"
        "- startSeconds, endSeconds: where it sits (a loop starting inside the attack sounds wrong; one ending past the strong body loops the fade).\n"
        "- startPitchHz, endPitchHz: the pitch at each end (they should match each other, and the expected pitch; a gap of more than "
        "about 0.5% is an audible jump).\n"
        "- levelWobbleDb: how much the level moves inside the loop (a few dB is natural movement; much more will be heard as pumping).\n"
        "- brightnessMatch: how alike the tone (the share of high frequencies) is at the two ends (1 = same; under 0.85 the tone jumps).\n"
        "Candidate 0, when listed, is the loop the sample has now.\n\n"
        "Pick for each sample the candidate that should sound smoothest held, weighing all of them (not only the score): "
        "prefer matched pitch, level and brightness at the seam, then length (longer is better when the sound is steady), "
        "then correlation. Choose the crossfade in milliseconds (20..500): short (20..60) for pure, steady tones (organ, "
        "flute, sine-like synths); medium (60..150) for most instruments; long (150..400) for noisy, chorused, ensemble, "
        "breathy or evolving sounds and for loops whose ends match less well. Answer -1 when no candidate is usable "
        "(a sound that dies away without sustaining, such as a pluck or a drum: it should play without a loop).\n\n"
        "Answer with JSON only, no other text:\n"
        "{\"samples\":[{\"index\":<the sample's index>,\"candidate\":<its number, 0 to keep its loop, -1 for none>,"
        "\"crossfadeMs\":<20..500>,\"why\":\"<one short sentence>\"}]}\n"
        "Give one entry for every sample, in any order.";
}

juce::String SfzLoops::aiRequest (const std::vector<AiSample>& samples)
{
    juce::String text;
    text << "Choose the loop (and crossfade) for each of these " << static_cast<int> (samples.size()) << " samples.\n";

    const auto describe = [] (juce::String& out, int numberShown, const LoopFinder::Candidate& c, double rate)
    {
        out << "  candidate " << numberShown << ": start " << juce::String (c.loopStart) << ", end " << juce::String (c.loopEnd)
            << ", score " << number (c.score, 3) << ", correlation " << number (c.correlation, 3)
            << ", levelMatch " << number (c.levelMatch, 3) << ", valueMatch " << number (c.valueMatch, 3)
            << ", slopeMatch " << number (c.slopeMatch, 3)
            << ", seconds " << number (c.seconds > 0.0 ? c.seconds : static_cast<double> (c.loopEnd - c.loopStart) / rate, 3)
            << ", periods " << number (c.periods, 1)
            << ", startSeconds " << number (c.startSeconds, 3) << ", endSeconds " << number (c.endSeconds, 3)
            << ", startPitchHz " << number (c.startPitchHz, 2) << ", endPitchHz " << number (c.endPitchHz, 2)
            << ", levelWobbleDb " << number (c.levelWobbleDb, 2) << ", brightnessMatch " << number (c.brightnessMatch, 3) << "\n";
    };

    for (const auto& s : samples)
    {
        const auto& f = s.found;
        text << "\nSample index " << s.index << ": \"" << s.name << "\", key " << Sfz::keyName (s.keycenter) << " (" << s.keycenter
             << ", expected " << number (keyHz (s.keycenter), 2) << " Hz), velocities " << s.lovel << "-" << s.hivel
             << ", " << number (s.seconds, 2) << " s, " << s.channels << (s.channels == 1 ? " channel" : " channels")
             << ", rate " << juce::String (juce::roundToInt (f.sampleRate)) << " Hz";

        if (f.success)
            text << ", detected pitch " << number (f.pitchHz, 2) << " Hz, peak " << number (f.peakLevelDb, 1) << " dB"
                 << ", sustain " << number (static_cast<double> (f.sustainStart) / f.sampleRate, 3) << "-"
                 << number (static_cast<double> (f.sustainEnd) / f.sampleRate, 3) << " s, strong body ends "
                 << number (static_cast<double> (f.bodyEnd) / f.sampleRate, 3) << " s";
        else if (f.error.isNotEmpty())
            text << ", the loop finder says: " << f.error;

        text << "\n";

        if (s.hasCurrent)
            describe (text, 0, s.current, f.sampleRate);

        for (size_t i = 0; i < f.candidates.size(); ++i)
            describe (text, static_cast<int> (i) + 1, f.candidates[i], f.sampleRate);

        if (! s.hasCurrent && f.candidates.empty())
            text << "  (no candidates)\n";
    }

    return text;
}

std::vector<SfzLoops::AiPick> SfzLoops::aiPicks (const juce::var& answer, juce::String& why)
{
    std::vector<AiPick> picks;
    juce::String text = answer.getProperty ("reply", {}).toString();

    if (const auto* blocks = answer.getProperty ("content", {}).getArray())
        for (const auto& block : *blocks)
            if (block.getProperty ("type", {}).toString() == "text")
                text << block.getProperty ("text", {}).toString() << "\n";

    const auto start = text.indexOfChar ('{');
    const auto end = text.lastIndexOfChar ('}');

    if (start < 0 || end <= start)
    {
        why = "Fanan AI didn't answer with loop picks this time. Please try again.";
        return picks;
    }

    const auto parsed = juce::JSON::parse (text.substring (start, end + 1));

    if (const auto* list = parsed.getProperty ("samples", {}).getArray())
    {
        for (const auto& item : *list)
        {
            AiPick pick;
            pick.index = static_cast<int> (item.getProperty ("index", -1));
            pick.candidate = static_cast<int> (item.getProperty ("candidate", -1));
            pick.crossfadeMs = juce::jlimit (20, 500, static_cast<int> (item.getProperty ("crossfadeMs", 100)));
            pick.why = item.getProperty ("why", {}).toString().substring (0, 240);

            if (pick.index >= 0)
                picks.push_back (pick);
        }
    }

    if (picks.empty())
        why = "Fanan AI didn't answer with loop picks this time. Please try again.";

    return picks;
}

// D:\workspace\Fanan_web_hub\src\SfzLoops.h

#pragma once

#include <juce_audio_basics/juce_audio_basics.h>
#include <juce_core/juce_core.h>

#include "LoopFinder.h"

#include <vector>

//==============================================================================
/**
    The Sampling Studio's Loop Editor (Sampler Arena's WaveformLoopEditor), its work away from
    the page: an SFZ read with each region's sample, keys, velocities and loop; saved again with
    the loops as set; the loops put in the samples' WAVs; and Fanan AI's help picking loops.

    Unlike Sampler Arena's, Save changes nothing in the SFZ but the loops of the regions whose
    loop was changed: every other opcode, header, comment and line stays as it was (Sampler Arena
    wrote the file anew with only six opcodes a region). Regions may use <group>, <global> and
    <master> (their keys, velocities, samples and loops are inherited), <control>'s default_path,
    key=, and note names (c4). Save As into another folder keeps the samples found (their paths,
    or default_path, made relative to the new folder).

    Ask Fanan AI: for each sample, the loop finder's candidates (and its loop now, if it has one)
    with what describes each (LoopFinder::Candidate) go to Fanan AI, which picks the loop that
    should sound smoothest held (or none, for a sound that doesn't sustain) and the crossfade.
    Only when asked; it uses credits.
*/
namespace SfzLoops
{
    struct Region
    {
        juce::String sample;                    // as the SFZ names it
        juce::File file;                        // where it is
        int lokey = 0, hikey = 127, keycenter = 60, lovel = 0, hivel = 127;

        bool looped = false;
        juce::String loopMode;                  // as read (loop_sustain when Sonify writes it)
        juce::int64 loopStart = 0, loopEnd = 0;
        int crossfade = 0;                      // samples
        bool changed = false;                   // Save writes its loop
        bool inheritedLoop = false;             // a <group> (or <global>) loops it

        // Where it is in the text (Patch::text).
        int headerStart = 0, bodyStart = 0, bodyEnd = 0;

        struct Opcode
        {
            juce::String name;
            int start = 0, valueStart = 0, end = 0;
        };

        std::vector<Opcode> own;                // its own opcodes
    };

    struct Patch
    {
        juce::File file;
        juce::String text;                      // as read, its line ends made \n
        bool crlf = false;                      // written back with CR LF
        std::vector<Region> regions;

        struct PathOpcode
        {
            int valueStart = 0, end = 0;
            juce::File points;                  // what it names (default_path: a folder)
            bool isDefaultPath = false;
            bool backslash = false;
        };

        std::vector<PathOpcode> paths;          // sample= and default_path=, wherever they are
    };

    /** Reads an SFZ (false, with why, when it can't be read or has no region). */
    bool load (const juce::File& sfz, Patch& patch, juce::String& why);

    /** The SFZ's text with every changed region's loop as set, its paths right for target's folder. */
    juce::String textFor (const Patch& patch, const juce::File& target);

    /** Writes the SFZ to target (as it was read: line ends, encoding), then each looped sample's
        loop into its WAV's smpl chunk (and a loop removed, out of it); the patch is read again
        from target. */
    juce::Result save (Patch& patch, const juce::File& target);

    /** A sample's waveform for the page: { channels, frames, rate, peaks: [[min, max...] each
        channel] }, each a whole number -127..127, buckets of them. */
    juce::var peaks (const juce::AudioBuffer<float>& audio, double sampleRate, int buckets = 1600);

    /** A key's frequency (equal temperament, A4 = 440 Hz). */
    double keyHz (int note);

    //==============================================================================
    /** What Fanan AI is told about one sample. */
    struct AiSample
    {
        int index = 0;                          // its region
        juce::String name;
        int keycenter = 60, lovel = 0, hivel = 127, channels = 1;
        double seconds = 0.0;
        LoopFinder::Result found;               // its candidates (1..)
        bool hasCurrent = false;
        LoopFinder::Candidate current;          // its loop now (0)
    };

    /** Fanan AI's pick for a sample: candidate 1.. one found, 0 its loop now, -1 no loop. */
    struct AiPick
    {
        int index = -1, candidate = -1, crossfadeMs = 100;
        juce::String why;
    };

    juce::String aiGuide();
    juce::String aiRequest (const std::vector<AiSample>& samples);
    std::vector<AiPick> aiPicks (const juce::var& answer, juce::String& why);

    /** How many samples go in one request (more: several requests, each charged). */
    constexpr int aiSamplesPerRequest = 24;
}

// D:\workspace\Fanan_web_hub\src\ShapeDoc.cpp
// From KnobMaker (C:\workspace\knobmaker); in Stella the shape inventory is in Documents\Sonify AI
// Studio\Shapes.

/*
    ShapeDoc.cpp
*/

#include "ShapeDoc.h"
#include "Settings.h"

#include <cmath>

namespace
{
    constexpr float kTwoPi = juce::MathConstants<float>::twoPi;

    float wrapAngle (float a) noexcept
    {
        while (a <  0.0f)    a += kTwoPi;
        while (a >= kTwoPi)  a -= kTwoPi;

        return a;
    }

    struct ArcSpec
    {
        juce::Point<float> centre;
        float radius = 0.0f, start = 0.0f, sweep = 0.0f;
        bool ok = false;
    };

    /** The unique circular arc that leaves `p` along `tangent` and ends at
        `target`. Two points and a tangent determine one circle. */
    ArcSpec arcFrom (juce::Point<float> p, juce::Point<float> tangent, juce::Point<float> target)
    {
        ArcSpec a;

        const juce::Point<float> nrm (-tangent.y, tangent.x);
        const auto m = target - p;

        const float denom = 2.0f * (nrm.x * m.x + nrm.y * m.y);

        if (std::abs (denom) < 1.0e-7f)
            return a;                       // target lies along the tangent: straight

        const float k = (m.x * m.x + m.y * m.y) / denom;

        a.centre = p + nrm * k;
        a.radius = std::abs (k);

        if (a.radius < 1.0e-6f || a.radius > 1.0e5f)
            return a;

        a.start = std::atan2 (p.y - a.centre.y, p.x - a.centre.x);

        const float endAngle = std::atan2 (target.y - a.centre.y, target.x - a.centre.x);

        // Which way round: the counter-clockwise tangent at the start angle
        // either agrees with the direction we were told to leave in, or it does
        // not, and that decides the sign of the sweep.
        const juce::Point<float> ccw (-std::sin (a.start), std::cos (a.start));

        a.sweep = wrapAngle (endAngle - a.start);

        if ((ccw.x * tangent.x + ccw.y * tangent.y) <= 0.0f)
            a.sweep -= kTwoPi;

        a.ok = true;
        return a;
    }

    void emitArc (juce::Path& path, const ArcSpec& a, float from, float sweep)
    {
        const int steps = juce::jlimit (4, 64, (int) std::lround (std::abs (sweep) * 20.0f));

        for (int i = 1; i <= steps; ++i)
        {
            const float t = from + sweep * ((float) i / (float) steps);
            path.lineTo (a.centre.x + std::cos (t) * a.radius,
                         a.centre.y + std::sin (t) * a.radius);
        }
    }

    /** Appends the curve from `from` through `via` to `to`, as a BIARC: two
        circular arcs meeting at `via` with a common tangent parallel to the
        chord.

        This is what gives the via point's position along the span a meaning.
        A single circle through three points is still a circle wherever you put
        the middle one — sliding it along only moves the circle. A biarc gives
        each half its own radius, computed from how far that half has to travel:
        park the point equidistant and both radii match, so the two halves are
        one circle and it reads as a true round. Slide it toward one end and
        that half tightens while the other goes lazy, which is the oval you get
        between a corner and an arc.

        The tangent is taken parallel to the chord because that is what the
        symmetric case demands — at the apex of a circular bulge the tangent IS
        parallel to the chord — so the round case falls out exactly rather than
        being approximated. */
    bool appendArc (juce::Path& path,
                    juce::Point<float> from, juce::Point<float> via, juce::Point<float> to)
    {
        const auto chord = to - from;
        const float length = chord.getDistanceFromOrigin();

        if (length < 1.0e-6f)
            return false;

        const juce::Point<float> dir (chord.x / length, chord.y / length);

        // The second half leaves `via` along the chord; the first half arrives
        // there, so it is computed backwards and drawn in reverse.
        const auto second = arcFrom (via, dir, to);
        const auto first  = arcFrom (via, { -dir.x, -dir.y }, from);

        if (! first.ok && ! second.ok)
            return false;

        if (first.ok) emitArc (path, first, first.start + first.sweep, -first.sweep);
        else          path.lineTo (via);

        if (second.ok) emitArc (path, second, second.start, second.sweep);
        else           path.lineTo (to);

        return true;
    }
}

//==============================================================================
juce::StringArray nodeModeNames()
{
    return { "Corner", "Arc" };
}

//==============================================================================
juce::Path ShapeDoc::buildPath() const
{
    juce::Path path;

    const int n = (int) nodes.size();

    if (n < 2)
        return path;

    auto at = [this, n] (int i) -> const ShapeNode& { return nodes[(size_t) (((i % n) + n) % n)]; };

    // An open path cannot bow its endpoints — an arc needs a neighbour on each
    // side — so they behave as corners however they are set.
    auto modeOf = [this, n, &at] (int i)
    {
        if (! closed && (i == 0 || i == n - 1))
            return NodeMode::Corner;

        return at (i).mode;
    };

    // Where one node's contribution hands over to the next. A corner owns the
    // handover point outright, because the outline genuinely passes through it.
    // Two arcs side by side split the difference, which is what lets a run of
    // arc points curve continuously instead of fighting over a shared end.
    auto boundary = [&at, &modeOf] (int i, int j)
    {
        const bool a = modeOf (i) == NodeMode::Arc;
        const bool b = modeOf (j) == NodeMode::Arc;

        if (a && b) return (at (i).pos + at (j).pos) * 0.5f;
        if (a)      return at (j).pos;

        return at (i).pos;
    };

    // Every node is visited exactly once, and only ever reads its OWN mode.
    //
    // The previous version walked the ring consuming two nodes per arc — the
    // via point and its far end — so whether a node's Arc setting was honoured
    // depended on the parity of where the walk happened to be when it arrived.
    // Two points placed symmetrically could therefore behave differently, which
    // is exactly the fault this replaces.
    bool started = false;

    auto moveTo = [&path, &started] (juce::Point<float> p)
    {
        if (! started) { path.startNewSubPath (p); started = true; }
        else           { path.lineTo (p); }
    };

    for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i)
    {
        if (modeOf (i) != NodeMode::Arc)
        {
            moveTo (at (i).pos);
            continue;
        }

        const auto entry = boundary (i - 1, i);
        const auto exit  = boundary (i, i + 1);

        moveTo (entry);

        if (! appendArc (path, entry, at (i).pos, exit))
        {
            // Too near a straight line to define a circle: two segments through
            // the node rather than a circumcentre out at infinity.
            path.lineTo (at (i).pos);
            path.lineTo (exit);
        }
    }

    if (closed)
        path.closeSubPath();

    return path;
}

//==============================================================================
juce::String ShapeDoc::toString() const
{
    juce::StringArray parts;

    parts.add (closed ? "closed" : "open");

    for (const auto& node : nodes)
        parts.add (juce::String (node.pos.x, 5) + "," + juce::String (node.pos.y, 5)
                     + "," + juce::String ((int) node.mode));

    return parts.joinIntoString (";");
}

ShapeDoc ShapeDoc::fromString (const juce::String& text)
{
    ShapeDoc doc;

    juce::StringArray parts;
    parts.addTokens (text, ";", {});
    parts.removeEmptyStrings();

    if (parts.isEmpty())
        return doc;

    int first = 0;

    if (parts[0] == "closed" || parts[0] == "open")
    {
        doc.closed = (parts[0] == "closed");
        first = 1;
    }

    for (int i = first; i < parts.size(); ++i)
    {
        juce::StringArray f;
        f.addTokens (parts[i], ",", {});

        if (f.size() < 2)
            continue;

        ShapeNode node;
        node.pos = { f[0].getFloatValue(), f[1].getFloatValue() };

        if (f.size() > 2)
            node.mode = (NodeMode) juce::jlimit (0, (int) NodeMode::numModes - 1,
                                                 f[2].getIntValue());

        doc.nodes.push_back (node);
    }

    return doc;
}

ShapeDoc ShapeDoc::pointerExample()
{
    // The Davies 1900H silhouette: a round skirt with a sharp nose. Five nodes
    // and three arcs, which is the case the whole editor exists for.
    ShapeDoc doc;
    doc.name = "Pointer";

    doc.nodes = { { { 0.50f, 0.06f }, NodeMode::Corner },   // nose
                  { { 0.72f, 0.30f }, NodeMode::Arc    },   // right shoulder
                  { { 0.94f, 0.66f }, NodeMode::Corner },
                  { { 0.50f, 0.96f }, NodeMode::Arc    },   // skirt
                  { { 0.06f, 0.66f }, NodeMode::Corner },
                  { { 0.28f, 0.30f }, NodeMode::Arc    } }; // left shoulder

    return doc;
}

namespace
{
    int libraryRevision = 0;
}

juce::File ShapeLibrary::folder()
{
    // Beside the Plugins Creator Studio's primitives, looks and textures.
    return Settings::getDataFolder().getChildFile ("Shapes");
}

juce::StringArray ShapeLibrary::names()
{
    juce::StringArray out;

    auto dir = folder();

    if (! dir.isDirectory())
        return out;

    juce::Array<juce::File> files;
    dir.findChildFiles (files, juce::File::findFiles, false, "*.fkshape");

    for (const auto& f : files)
        out.add (f.getFileNameWithoutExtension());

    out.sort (true);
    return out;
}

ShapeDoc ShapeLibrary::load (const juce::String& name)
{
    auto file = folder().getChildFile (juce::File::createLegalFileName (name) + ".fkshape");

    if (! file.existsAsFile())
        return {};

    auto doc = ShapeDoc::fromString (file.loadFileAsString());
    doc.name = name;
    return doc;
}

bool ShapeLibrary::save (const ShapeDoc& doc)
{
    if (doc.name.isEmpty())
        return false;

    auto dir = folder();
    dir.createDirectory();

    auto file = dir.getChildFile (juce::File::createLegalFileName (doc.name) + ".fkshape");

    if (! file.replaceWithText (doc.toString()))
        return false;

    ++libraryRevision;
    return true;
}

bool ShapeLibrary::remove (const juce::String& name)
{
    auto file = folder().getChildFile (juce::File::createLegalFileName (name) + ".fkshape");

    if (! file.existsAsFile() || ! file.deleteFile())
        return false;

    ++libraryRevision;
    return true;
}

int ShapeLibrary::revision()
{
    return libraryRevision;
}

// D:\workspace\Fanan_web_hub\src\ShapeDoc.h
// From KnobMaker (C:\workspace\knobmaker); in Stella the inventory's folder is the studio's own.

/*
    ShapeDoc.h

    A hand-drawn outline, and the inventory of them.

    The model is a single closed ring of nodes. Each node is either a CORNER —
    the outline passes through it with straight segments either side — or an
    ARC, where the span from the previous node to the next bows through it as a
    true circle.

    That second one is the whole point of the editor. Three points define
    exactly one circle, so "bow this span through here" is a circumcircle, not
    an approximation built out of tangent handles. It is what lets a Davies-style
    pointer knob be five points and two drags instead of a fight with a pen tool.

    Static and Corner are the same geometry: a node the outline passes through
    with straight segments IS a tip. The editor still offers both, because the
    distinction is about what dragging does, not about what gets drawn.
*/

#pragma once

#include <juce_gui_basics/juce_gui_basics.h>

#include <vector>

//==============================================================================
enum class NodeMode
{
    Corner = 0,   ///< straight in, straight out — a plain vertex or a tip
    Arc,          ///< the span through this node bows as a circle
    numModes
};

juce::StringArray nodeModeNames();

//==============================================================================
struct ShapeNode
{
    juce::Point<float> pos;                 ///< normalised, 0..1 across the grid
    NodeMode mode = NodeMode::Corner;
};

//==============================================================================
struct ShapeDoc
{
    juce::String name { "Untitled" };
    std::vector<ShapeNode> nodes;
    bool closed = true;

    /** Builds the outline in normalised 0..1 space. Arc nodes become circular
        sweeps through their neighbours; anything too near collinear to define a
        circle falls back to a straight line rather than flying off to a
        circumcentre at infinity. */
    juce::Path buildPath() const;

    bool isEmpty() const noexcept { return nodes.size() < 2; }

    juce::String toString() const;
    static ShapeDoc fromString (const juce::String&);

    /** A Davies-style pointer: round skirt, sharp nose. Also the worked example
        for what the editor is for. */
    static ShapeDoc pointerExample();
    static ShapeDoc teardropExample();
    static ShapeDoc arrowExample();

    static juce::StringArray exampleNames();
    static ShapeDoc exampleByIndex (int);
};

//==============================================================================
/** The inventory: named shapes on disk, shared by every document. */
namespace ShapeLibrary
{
    /** Stella: <user data>/Plugins Creator/Shapes */
    juce::File folder();

    juce::StringArray names();

    /** Invalid-but-empty ShapeDoc when the name is not on disk. */
    ShapeDoc load (const juce::String& name);

    bool save (const ShapeDoc&);
    bool remove (const juce::String& name);

    /** Bumped on every save or delete, so a panel can tell its list is stale. */
    int revision();
}

// D:\workspace\Fanan_web_hub\src\ShapeEditor.cpp
// From KnobMaker (C:\workspace\knobmaker), unchanged: the same layer builder in both apps.

/*
    ShapeEditor.cpp
*/

#include "ShapeEditor.h"

namespace
{
    constexpr float kNodeHit = 9.0f;
    constexpr float kSpanHit = 7.0f;

    // Long enough to catch a deliberate second click, short enough that the menu
    // does not feel like it is lagging.
    constexpr int kRightClickWindowMs = 260;
}

//==============================================================================
ShapeEditor::ShapeEditor()
{
    setWantsKeyboardFocus (true);
    shape = ShapeDoc::pointerExample();
}

void ShapeEditor::setShape (const ShapeDoc& s)
{
    shape = s;
    dragging = -1;
    selected = -1;
    repaint();
}

void ShapeEditor::setGrid (int divisions)
{
    gridDivisions = juce::jlimit (2, 64, divisions);
    repaint();
}

void ShapeEditor::setSnapEnabled (bool shouldSnap)
{
    snapping = shouldSnap;
}

void ShapeEditor::clearShape()
{
    shape.nodes.clear();
    dragging = selected = -1;
    changed();
}

void ShapeEditor::changed()
{
    repaint();

    if (onChange != nullptr)
        onChange();
}

//==============================================================================
juce::Rectangle<float> ShapeEditor::canvasArea() const
{
    // Square, because a shape is authored in a square and stretched by the
    // layer. Authoring it in a rectangle would bake the distortion in.
    auto r = getLocalBounds().toFloat().reduced (10.0f);
    const float side = juce::jmin (r.getWidth(), r.getHeight());

    return juce::Rectangle<float> (side, side).withCentre (r.getCentre());
}

juce::Point<float> ShapeEditor::toShape (juce::Point<float> screen) const
{
    auto r = canvasArea();

    return { juce::jlimit (0.0f, 1.0f, (screen.x - r.getX()) / juce::jmax (1.0f, r.getWidth())),
             juce::jlimit (0.0f, 1.0f, (screen.y - r.getY()) / juce::jmax (1.0f, r.getHeight())) };
}

juce::Point<float> ShapeEditor::toScreen (juce::Point<float> n) const
{
    auto r = canvasArea();
    return { r.getX() + n.x * r.getWidth(), r.getY() + n.y * r.getHeight() };
}

juce::Point<float> ShapeEditor::snap (juce::Point<float> n) const
{
    if (! snapping)
        return n;

    const float d = (float) gridDivisions;

    return { juce::jlimit (0.0f, 1.0f, std::round (n.x * d) / d),
             juce::jlimit (0.0f, 1.0f, std::round (n.y * d) / d) };
}

int ShapeEditor::nodeAt (juce::Point<float> screen) const
{
    for (int i = 0; i < (int) shape.nodes.size(); ++i)
        if (toScreen (shape.nodes[(size_t) i].pos).getDistanceFrom (screen) < kNodeHit)
            return i;

    return -1;
}

int ShapeEditor::spanAt (juce::Point<float> screen) const
{
    const int n = (int) shape.nodes.size();

    if (n < 2)
        return -1;

    const int last = shape.closed ? n : n - 1;

    for (int i = 0; i < last; ++i)
    {
        const auto a = toScreen (shape.nodes[(size_t) i].pos);
        const auto b = toScreen (shape.nodes[(size_t) ((i + 1) % n)].pos);

        // getDistanceFromPoint always writes back the nearest point on the line,
        // so it needs somewhere to put it even when we only want the distance.
        juce::Point<float> nearest;

        if (juce::Line<float> (a, b).getDistanceFromPoint (screen, nearest) < kSpanHit)
            return i;
    }

    return -1;
}

//==============================================================================
void ShapeEditor::paint (juce::Graphics& g)
{
    auto r = canvasArea();

    g.fillAll (juce::Colour (0xff1b1b1e));

    g.setColour (juce::Colour (0xff232327));
    g.fillRect (r);

    // Grid
    g.setColour (juce::Colour (0xff2c2c32));

    for (int i = 1; i < gridDivisions; ++i)
    {
        const float f = (float) i / (float) gridDivisions;
        g.drawVerticalLine   ((int) (r.getX() + f * r.getWidth()),  r.getY(), r.getBottom());
        g.drawHorizontalLine ((int) (r.getY() + f * r.getHeight()), r.getX(), r.getRight());
    }

    g.setColour (juce::Colour (0xff3a3a42));
    g.drawVerticalLine   ((int) r.getCentreX(), r.getY(), r.getBottom());
    g.drawHorizontalLine ((int) r.getCentreY(), r.getX(), r.getRight());
    g.drawRect (r, 1.0f);

    if (shape.nodes.size() >= 2)
    {
        auto path = shape.buildPath();
        path.applyTransform (juce::AffineTransform::scale (r.getWidth(), r.getHeight())
                                 .translated (r.getX(), r.getY()));

        g.setColour (juce::Colour (0x33e8c020));
        g.fillPath (path);

        g.setColour (juce::Colour (0xffe8c020));
        g.strokePath (path, juce::PathStrokeType (1.6f));
    }

    for (int i = 0; i < (int) shape.nodes.size(); ++i)
    {
        const auto& node = shape.nodes[(size_t) i];
        const auto p = toScreen (node.pos);

        // Arc nodes draw round, corners square — the same language the contour
        // editor uses, so the shape of the marker tells you what it does.
        const bool isArc = node.mode == NodeMode::Arc;

        g.setColour (i == selected ? juce::Colour (0xffff6b6b)
                                   : (isArc ? juce::Colour (0xff8fd0ff)
                                            : juce::Colour (0xffe8c020)));

        if (isArc) g.fillEllipse (p.x - 4.5f, p.y - 4.5f, 9.0f, 9.0f);
        else       g.fillRect (p.x - 4.0f, p.y - 4.0f, 8.0f, 8.0f);

        if (i == 0)
        {
            g.setColour (juce::Colours::white.withAlpha (0.85f));
            g.drawEllipse (p.x - 7.5f, p.y - 7.5f, 15.0f, 15.0f, 1.2f);
        }
    }

    if (shape.nodes.empty())
    {
        g.setColour (juce::Colours::grey);
        g.setFont (juce::Font (juce::FontOptions (13.0f)));
        g.drawText ("Double-click to place points.  Drag a point to move it.  "
                    "Right-click for Corner / Arc.",
                    r.reduced (16), juce::Justification::centred, true);
    }
}

//==============================================================================
void ShapeEditor::mouseDown (const juce::MouseEvent& e)
{
    const int node = nodeAt (e.position);

    if (e.mods.isPopupMenu())
    {
        if (node < 0)
            return;

        selected = node;
        repaint();

        const auto now = juce::Time::getMillisecondCounter();

        // Second right-click on the same point, before the menu had a chance to
        // open: that is the delete gesture.
        if (isTimerRunning() && node == lastRightNode
              && now - lastRightTime < (juce::uint32) (kRightClickWindowMs * 2))
        {
            stopTimer();
            pendingMenuNode = -1;
            lastRightNode = -1;
            deleteNode (node);
            return;
        }

        lastRightNode = node;
        lastRightTime = now;
        pendingMenuNode = node;
        pendingMenuPos = e.getScreenPosition();
        startTimer (kRightClickWindowMs);
        return;
    }

    selected = node;
    dragging = node;
    repaint();
}

void ShapeEditor::timerCallback()
{
    stopTimer();

    const int node = pendingMenuNode;
    pendingMenuNode = -1;

    if (node >= 0)
        showMenuFor (node, pendingMenuPos);
}

void ShapeEditor::deleteNode (int nodeIndex)
{
    if (nodeIndex < 0 || nodeIndex >= (int) shape.nodes.size())
        return;

    shape.nodes.erase (shape.nodes.begin() + nodeIndex);
    selected = -1;
    changed();
}

void ShapeEditor::mouseDrag (const juce::MouseEvent& e)
{
    if (dragging < 0 || dragging >= (int) shape.nodes.size())
        return;

    // Where the mouse is released IS the value. On an Arc node this is the
    // point the span bows through, so the curve follows the cursor exactly
    // rather than being inferred from a handle somewhere else.
    shape.nodes[(size_t) dragging].pos = snap (toShape (e.position));
    changed();
}

void ShapeEditor::mouseUp (const juce::MouseEvent&)
{
    dragging = -1;
}

void ShapeEditor::mouseDoubleClick (const juce::MouseEvent& e)
{
    const int node = nodeAt (e.position);

    if (node >= 0)
    {
        // Flip between the two behaviours without going to the menu.
        auto& m = shape.nodes[(size_t) node].mode;
        m = (m == NodeMode::Arc) ? NodeMode::Corner : NodeMode::Arc;
        changed();
        return;
    }

    const int span = spanAt (e.position);
    ShapeNode fresh;
    fresh.pos = snap (toShape (e.position));

    if (span >= 0)
    {
        // Dropped onto an existing span: go in between, so the ring keeps its
        // order. Appending would jump the outline across the shape.
        fresh.mode = NodeMode::Arc;
        shape.nodes.insert (shape.nodes.begin() + span + 1, fresh);
        selected = span + 1;
    }
    else
    {
        shape.nodes.push_back (fresh);
        selected = (int) shape.nodes.size() - 1;
    }

    changed();
}

//==============================================================================
void ShapeEditor::showMenuFor (int nodeIndex, juce::Point<int> screenPos)
{
    if (nodeIndex < 0 || nodeIndex >= (int) shape.nodes.size())
        return;

    const auto current = shape.nodes[(size_t) nodeIndex].mode;

    juce::PopupMenu m;
    m.addItem (1, "Corner", true, current == NodeMode::Corner);
    m.addItem (2, "Arc",    true, current == NodeMode::Arc);
    m.addSeparator();
    m.addItem (3, "Delete point", shape.nodes.size() > 2);

    juce::Component::SafePointer<ShapeEditor> safe (this);

    // Positioned where the click landed, not on the component — by the time
    // this opens the pointer has had a moment to be somewhere else.
    m.showMenuAsync (juce::PopupMenu::Options()
                         .withTargetScreenArea ({ screenPos.x, screenPos.y, 1, 1 }),
                     [safe, nodeIndex] (int result)
    {
        auto* self = safe.getComponent();

        if (self == nullptr || result == 0)
            return;

        if (nodeIndex >= (int) self->shape.nodes.size())
            return;

        if (result == 1)      self->shape.nodes[(size_t) nodeIndex].mode = NodeMode::Corner;
        else if (result == 2) self->shape.nodes[(size_t) nodeIndex].mode = NodeMode::Arc;
        else if (result == 3)
        {
            self->deleteNode (nodeIndex);
            return;
        }

        self->changed();
    });
}

// D:\workspace\Fanan_web_hub\src\ShapeEditor.h
// From KnobMaker (C:\workspace\knobmaker), unchanged: the same layer builder in both apps.

/*
    ShapeEditor.h

    The drawing surface for the shape inventory.

    Interaction, deliberately small:

      double-click empty space   add a node at the end of the ring
      double-click a span        insert a node into that span
      drag a node                move it — and if it is an Arc node, the span
                                 through it bows to wherever you release
      right-click a node         Corner / Arc / Delete
      right-click it twice       delete it outright
      double-click a node        toggle Corner and Arc

    There are no tangent handles anywhere, and that is the entire design. A span
    that bows through the node you are dragging is a circle through three points,
    which needs no handles to specify and cannot be dragged into the twisted
    shapes a pen tool produces when the two arms disagree.
*/

#pragma once

#include "ShapeDoc.h"

#include <functional>

//==============================================================================
class ShapeEditor final : public juce::Component,
                          private juce::Timer
{
public:
    ShapeEditor();

    void setShape (const ShapeDoc&);
    const ShapeDoc& getShape() const noexcept { return shape; }

    void setGrid (int divisions);
    void setSnapEnabled (bool);

    /** Removes every node. */
    void clearShape();

    std::function<void()> onChange;

    void paint (juce::Graphics&) override;

    void mouseDown (const juce::MouseEvent&) override;
    void mouseDrag (const juce::MouseEvent&) override;
    void mouseUp (const juce::MouseEvent&) override;
    void mouseDoubleClick (const juce::MouseEvent&) override;

private:
    juce::Rectangle<float> canvasArea() const;
    juce::Point<float> toShape (juce::Point<float> screen) const;
    juce::Point<float> toScreen (juce::Point<float> normalised) const;
    juce::Point<float> snap (juce::Point<float> normalised) const;

    int nodeAt (juce::Point<float> screen) const;
    int spanAt (juce::Point<float> screen) const;

    void timerCallback() override;
    void showMenuFor (int nodeIndex, juce::Point<int> screenPos);
    void deleteNode (int nodeIndex);
    void changed();

    ShapeDoc shape;

    int  gridDivisions = 16;
    bool snapping = true;

    int dragging = -1;
    int selected = -1;

    // A right-click cannot both open a menu and wait to see whether a second one
    // is coming: the open menu takes the modal state and swallows the second
    // click before this component ever sees it. So the menu is held back just
    // long enough to find out, and a second click within that window deletes
    // instead.
    int  pendingMenuNode = -1;
    juce::Point<int> pendingMenuPos;
    int  lastRightNode = -1;
    juce::uint32 lastRightTime = 0;

    JUCE_DECLARE_NON_COPYABLE_WITH_LEAK_DETECTOR (ShapeEditor)
};

ShapeWorkspace::ShapeWorkspace()

    addAndMakeVisible (editor);

    editor.onChange = [this]

        status (juce::String (editor.getShape().nodes.size()) + " points");
    };

    list.setRowHeight (24);
    list.setColour (juce::ListBox::backgroundColourId, juce::Colour (0xff202023));

    nameLabel.setColour (juce::Label::textColourId, juce::Colour (0xffc0c0c4));
    nameLabel.setFont (juce::Font (juce::FontOptions (12.0f)));

    nameBox.setText ("Pointer", juce::dontSendNotification);
    addAndMakeVisible (nameBox);

    newButton.onClick    = [this] { editor.clearShape(); nameBox.setText ("Untitled",
                                                                          juce::dontSendNotification);
                                    status ("Empty shape — double-click to place points"); };

    deleteButton.onClick = [this] { deleteSelected(); };
    folderButton.onClick = [this]
    {
        auto f = ShapeLibrary::folder();

        f.revealToUser();

    for (auto* b : { &newButton, &saveButton, &deleteButton, &folderButton })
        addAndMakeVisible (b);

    gridLabel.setColour (juce::Label::textColourId, juce::Colour (0xffc0c0c4));
    gridLabel.setFont (juce::Font (juce::FontOptions (12.0f)));
    addAndMakeVisible (gridLabel);

    gridSlider.setSliderStyle (juce::Slider::IncDecButtons);
    gridSlider.setRange (2.0, 64.0, 1.0);
    gridSlider.setValue (16.0, juce::dontSendNotification);
    gridSlider.setTextBoxStyle (juce::Slider::TextBoxLeft, false, 46, 20);
    gridSlider.onValueChange = [this] { editor.setGrid ((int) gridSlider.getValue()); };
    addAndMakeVisible (gridSlider);

    snapButton.setToggleState (true, juce::dontSendNotification);
    snapButton.onClick = [this] { editor.setSnapEnabled (snapButton.getToggleState()); };
    addAndMakeVisible (snapButton);

    exampleLabel.setColour (juce::Label::textColourId, juce::Colour (0xffc0c0c4));
    exampleLabel.setFont (juce::Font (juce::FontOptions (12.0f)));
    addAndMakeVisible (exampleLabel);

    exampleBox.addItemList (ShapeDoc::exampleNames(), 1);
    exampleBox.setSelectedId (1, juce::dontSendNotification);
    exampleBox.onChange = [this]
    {
        auto doc = ShapeDoc::exampleByIndex (exampleBox.getSelectedId() - 1);
        editor.setShape (doc);
        nameBox.setText (doc.name, juce::dontSendNotification);
        status ("Loaded example: " + doc.name);
    };
    addAndMakeVisible (exampleBox);

    statusLabel.setColour (juce::Label::textColourId, juce::Colours::grey);
    statusLabel.setFont (juce::Font (juce::FontOptions (12.0f)));
    addAndMakeVisible (statusLabel);

    configurePanelControls (*this);

    editor.setShape (ShapeDoc::pointerExample());
    refreshInventory();
    status ("Double-click to place points.  Right-click a point for Corner / Arc.");
}

//==============================================================================
void ShapeWorkspace::status (const juce::String& text)
{
    statusLabel.setText (text, juce::dontSendNotification);

    if (onStatus != nullptr)
        onStatus (text);
}

void ShapeWorkspace::refreshInventory()
{
    inventory = ShapeLibrary::names();
    list.updateContent();
    list.repaint();
}

//==============================================================================
void ShapeWorkspace::saveCurrent()
{
    auto doc = editor.getShape();
    doc.name = nameBox.getText().trim();

    if (doc.name.isEmpty())
    {
        status ("Give the shape a name first.");
        return;
    }

    if (doc.nodes.size() < 2)
    {
        status ("A shape needs at least two points.");
        return;
    }

    if (! ShapeLibrary::save (doc))
    {
        status ("Could not write the shape to " + ShapeLibrary::folder().getFullPathName());
        return;
    }

    refreshInventory();
    status ("Saved \"" + doc.name + "\" — Shape layers referring to it update straight away.");
}

void ShapeWorkspace::deleteSelected()
{
    const int row = list.getSelectedRow();

    if (row < 0 || row >= inventory.size())
    {
        status ("Select a shape in the inventory first.");
        return;
    }

    const auto name = inventory[row];

    juce::Component::SafePointer<ShapeWorkspace> safe (this);

    juce::AlertWindow::showOkCancelBox (
        juce::MessageBoxIconType::QuestionIcon,
        "Delete shape",
        "Delete \"" + name + "\"? Layers referring to it will fall back to a plain outline.",
        "Delete", "Cancel", this,
        juce::ModalCallbackFunction::create ([safe, name] (int result)
        {
            if (result != 1)
                return;

            if (auto* self = safe.getComponent())
            {
                ShapeLibrary::remove (name);
                self->refreshInventory();
                self->status ("Deleted \"" + name + "\"");
            }
        }));
}

//==============================================================================
int ShapeWorkspace::getNumRows()
{
    return inventory.size();
}

void ShapeWorkspace::paintListBoxItem (int row, juce::Graphics& g, int w, int h, bool selected)
{
    if (row < 0 || row >= inventory.size())
        return;

    if (selected)
    {
        g.setColour (juce::Colour (0xff3a5a7a));
        g.fillRect (0, 0, w, h);
    }

    // A thumbnail of the outline, because a list of names tells you nothing
    // about shapes.
    auto doc = ShapeLibrary::load (inventory[row]);

    if (! doc.isEmpty())
    {
        auto path = doc.buildPath();
        const float side = (float) h - 6.0f;
        path.applyTransform (juce::AffineTransform::scale (side, side).translated (4.0f, 3.0f));

        g.setColour (juce::Colour (0xffe8c020));
        g.fillPath (path);
    }

    g.setColour (juce::Colour (0xffd8d8dc));
    g.setFont (juce::Font (juce::FontOptions (13.0f)));
    g.drawText (inventory[row], h + 8, 0, w - h - 12, h, juce::Justification::centredLeft, true);
}

void ShapeWorkspace::listBoxItemClicked (int row, const juce::MouseEvent&)
{
    if (row < 0 || row >= inventory.size())
        return;

    auto doc = ShapeLibrary::load (inventory[row]);

    if (doc.isEmpty())
    {
        status ("\"" + inventory[row] + "\" could not be read.");
        return;
    }

    editor.setShape (doc);
    nameBox.setText (doc.name, juce::dontSendNotification);
    status ("Editing \"" + doc.name + "\"");
}

//==============================================================================
void ShapeWorkspace::paint (juce::Graphics& g)
{
    g.fillAll (juce::Colour (0xff1e1e21));
}

void ShapeWorkspace::resized()
{
    auto area = getLocalBounds().reduced (8);

    statusLabel.setBounds (area.removeFromBottom (20));
    area.removeFromBottom (6);

    auto right = area.removeFromRight (280);
    area.removeFromRight (8);

    {
        auto bar = area.removeFromTop (26);
        exampleLabel.setBounds (bar.removeFromLeft (70));
        exampleBox.setBounds (bar.removeFromLeft (130));
        bar.removeFromLeft (16);
        gridLabel.setBounds (bar.removeFromLeft (40));
        gridSlider.setBounds (bar.removeFromLeft (110));
        bar.removeFromLeft (10);
        snapButton.setBounds (bar.removeFromLeft (130));
    }

    area.removeFromTop (6);
    editor.setBounds (area);

    {
        auto bar = right.removeFromTop (26);
        nameLabel.setBounds (bar.removeFromLeft (46));
        nameBox.setBounds (bar);
    }

    right.removeFromTop (6);

    {
        auto bar = right.removeFromTop (26);
        newButton.setBounds (bar.removeFromLeft (60));
        bar.removeFromLeft (6);
        saveButton.setBounds (bar);
    }

    right.removeFromTop (6);

    {
        auto bar = right.removeFromBottom (26);
        deleteButton.setBounds (bar.removeFromLeft (80));
        bar.removeFromLeft (6);
        folderButton.setBounds (bar.removeFromLeft (80));
    }

    right.removeFromBottom (6);
    list.setBounds (right);
}

<!-- D:\workspace\Fanan_web_hub\src\skill_3d_displays.md -->
---
name: 3d-displays
for: plugins
title: 3D displays
description: Exciting 3D screens for plugin panels, built into the studio: an oscillator's waves as a lit 3D terrain (the wavetable look), two oscillators blending as one surface, the filter opening and closing as a rolling 3D sweep, and the sound itself as a live 3D waterfall (spectrum or wave). The part that plays is lit and glows while the instrument sounds, and the user turns them by dragging. Read it whenever a synth has two or more oscillators, a morph or wavetable knob, or when the user asks for 3D, a waterfall, a wavetable view, a live filter, or a more exciting screen.
---
# 3D displays

Four elements built into the studio, drawn in 3D: rows of curves stacked in depth, the nearer rows hiding the ones behind, seen in perspective from above. Each is a panel's hero screen: dark, glowing, alive while the instrument plays. The user drags to turn and tilt it (Shift: finely), the wheel zooms, a double-click puts it back. Nothing to program: place one with its name as the `"type"`, bind it, build.

## Which one
- **WaveTerrain**: one oscillator's waves along a knob (its morph, its wavetable position, its fold depth...): a row for each step of the knob, the row that plays lit white and glowing, gliding as the knob or its modulation moves it, with light rippling out from it while notes sound. The classic wavetable view.
- **MorphSurface**: two oscillators and the blend between them as one surface: oscillator A's wave along the front edge, B's along the back, the mix in between (B tuned against A twists the shapes as they blend), colours running from A's to B's, the mix row lit. The one for any synth with an A/B mix.
- **FilterSweep**: the filter's response now at the front and the moments before rolling back, so the filter visibly opens and closes as you play (an envelope sweep rises and falls like a wave rolling away); the cutoff is a bright point.
- **SoundWaterfall**: the sound itself, live: its spectrum (or its waveform, held steady on the note's cycle) rolling back from the front.

Two or more oscillators: a `MorphSurface` when there's a mix between A and B; otherwise a `WaveTerrain` for each oscillator side by side, each with its own `"label"` ("Osc 1", "Osc 2") and `"color"`. Add a `FilterSweep` beside them when the filter has an envelope or LFO. At most two 3D displays on a panel: each takes about 4 ms of every frame while it shows.

Sizes: 360 to 520 wide, 180 to 260 tall; a 2:1 box suits them. They draw their own dark background, so they sit best in a screen area of the panel (a recessed screen from the background-painter skill, or a dark group). Colours that glow on black: teal `#38E0D0`, magenta `#FF4FD8`, amber `#FFB347`, periwinkle `#7C9CFF`, lime `#B5E48C`; use the panel's accent for the main one (the panel-taste skill).

## Placing them
With `edit_layout`, like any element; every key but the type and the box is optional:
```json
{ "type": "WaveTerrain", "x": 24, "y": 64, "w": 420, "h": 210, "label": "Osc 1", "color": "#38E0D0",
  "params": { "timbre": "synth.timbre", "morph": "synth.morph" },
  "sources": { "position": "synth.morph", "level": "synth.env" },
  "settings": { "engine": "Analog", "sweep": "morph", "rows": 40 } }
{ "type": "MorphSurface", "x": 24, "y": 64, "w": 440, "h": 220, "label": "A / B", "color": "#38E0D0",
  "params": { "mix": "synth.mix", "timbreA": "synth.timbre", "morphA": "synth.morph",
              "timbreB": "synth.timbre2", "morphB": "synth.morph2", "tune": "synth.tune2" },
  "sources": { "mix": "synth.mix", "level": "synth.env" },
  "settings": { "engineA": "Analog", "engineB": "Fm", "colorB": "#FF4FD8" } }
{ "type": "FilterSweep", "x": 460, "y": 64, "w": 400, "h": 210, "label": "Filter", "color": "#FFB347",
  "params": { "cutoff": "synth.cutoff", "resonance": "synth.reso" },
  "sources": { "cutoff": "synth.cutoff", "level": "synth.env" },
  "settings": { "mode": "lowpass24" } }
{ "type": "SoundWaterfall", "x": 24, "y": 290, "w": 420, "h": 210, "label": "Output", "color": "#7C9CFF",
  "source": "plugin.out L", "settings": { "mode": "spectrum" } }
```
- `"params"` binds knobs by role. WaveTerrain: `"timbre"`, `"morph"`; `"sweep"` (`"morph"` or `"timbre"`) is the one along the depth, the other shapes every row, and its value shows under it. MorphSurface: `"mix"`, `"timbreA"`, `"morphA"`, `"timbreB"`, `"morphB"`, `"tune"` (B's tuning in semitones); a missing knob counts as half way. FilterSweep: `"cutoff"` (Hz, kHz or 0..1), `"resonance"`.
- `"settings"`: `"rows"` (WaveTerrain 40, MorphSurface 32, FilterSweep 36, SoundWaterfall 40; fewer is lighter), `"points"` (96), FilterSweep `"mode"` (`lowpass`, `lowpass24`, `highpass`, `highpass24`, `bandpass`), FilterSweep and SoundWaterfall `"speed"` (rows a second rolling back), SoundWaterfall `"mode"` (`"spectrum"` or `"wave"`), MorphSurface `"colorB"`.

## Making them live
They read live values by role from `"sources"`: a module's display (its value as the module shows it). Without one they follow the knobs, and glow while any key is held.
- `"position"` (WaveTerrain) / `"mix"` (MorphSurface): where it plays now, 0..1, modulation included (the knob plus its LFO or envelope).
- `"level"`: how loud it sounds, 0..1: the loudest voice's envelope (the synth-engines template shows it as `"synth.env"`).
- `"cutoff"` (FilterSweep): the live cutoff in Hz (the synth-engines template shows it as `"synth.cutoff"`). The toolbox's own `filter` curve takes the same display as its `"source"`, and then opens and closes as it plays too.
- SoundWaterfall watches a signal as its own `"source"`: `"plugin.out L"`, or a module's output.

A module shows values by naming them after `create` in its ModuleType and calling `display()` in `process()`, once per block:
```cpp
// The names, given to the registrar after create: { ..., displayNames, STELLA_COUNT (displayNames) }.
// In the layout they're "<moduleId>.env" and "<moduleId>.morph".
const char* const displayNames[] { "env", "morph" };

// In process(), once per block, after the samples:
display (0, loudestLevel);   // the loudest voice's envelope, 0..1
display (1, morphNow);       // the morph with its modulation (knob plus LFO), 0..1
```

## The waves are the sound's
`"engine"` (WaveTerrain) and `"engineA"`/`"engineB"` (MorphSurface) name the synth-engines struct the oscillator uses: `Analog`, `Supersaw`, `Morph`, `Fold`, `Fm`, `PhaseDistortion`, `Additive`, `Formant` (anything else: a sine). The display draws that engine's wave, shaped by the knobs bound as `"timbre"` and `"morph"` as they shape the sound, so match the engine to the code.

An oscillator of your own (a wavetable, a new shape) gets its own element drawn the same way: `#include "stella_view3d.h"` (the 3D view the built-ins use) and fill the rows from the oscillator's shape. Put the shape function in a header in `modules/` that doesn't include stella_api.h, call it from the oscillator, and include it in the element as `"../modules/<Name>.h"`: the picture is then exactly what plays.
```cpp
// elements/WaveScan.cpp: my oscillator's waves in 3D along its scan knob, the playing row lit.
#include "stella_view3d.h"
#include "../modules/ScanShape.h"   // float scanShape (float phase, float scan): -1..1

using namespace stella::ui;

class WaveScan final : public Element
{
public:
    void resized() override { cam.width = (float) width(); cam.height = (float) height(); }

    void paint (Canvas& g) override
    {
        const Colour accent = colour (0xff38e0d0);
        constexpr int rows = 40, points = 96;

        if (heights.empty())   // the rows, once: row r is the wave at scan r / (rows - 1)
            for (int r = 0; r < rows; ++r)
                for (int i = 0; i < points; ++i)
                    heights.push_back (scanShape ((float) i / (points - 1), (float) r / (rows - 1)));

        const float target = hasSource ("position") ? level ("position") : (hasParam ("scan") ? normalised ("scan") : 0.5f);
        position = view3d::glide (position, view3d::clamp (target, 0.0f, 1.0f));
        const float sounding = hasSource ("level") ? view3d::clamp (level ("level"), 0.0f, 1.0f) : 0.0f;
        glow = sounding > glow ? view3d::glide (glow, sounding, 0.6f) : glow * 0.92f;

        cam.fit (-0.6f, 0.15f);   // the box from the floor to the top, fitted to the element
        view3d::stage (g, cam, 0xff0d1117, 0xff050608, withAlpha (accent, 0.08f), -0.6f);

        view3d::terrain (g, cam, heights.data(), rows, points, 0.36f, -0.6f, [&] (int r)
        {
            const float d = (float) r - position * (rows - 1);
            const float lit = std::exp (-d * d / 0.8f);

            view3d::RowLook look;
            look.line = withAlpha (mix (mix (0xff1b3a40, accent, 0.3f), 0xfff2fffd, lit), 0.55f + 0.45f * lit);
            look.thickness = 1.0f + 1.4f * lit;
            look.glow = lit > 0.2f ? withAlpha (accent, (0.12f + 0.30f * glow) * lit) : 0u;
            look.glowWidth = 6.0f + 8.0f * glow;
            look.xray = lit > 0.5f ? 0.4f : 0.0f;   // the playing row shows through what's in front
            return look;
        });

        g.drawText (label(), 8.0f, (float) height() - 18.0f, (float) width() * 0.5f, 16.0f, 12.0f, 0xd8e6edf3, Align::left, true);
    }

    bool mouseDown (const Mouse& m) override         { orbit.down (cam, m); return true; }
    void mouseDrag (const Mouse& m) override         { orbit.drag (cam, m); }
    void mouseWheel (const Mouse&, float n) override { orbit.wheel (cam, n); }

private:
    view3d::Camera cam;
    view3d::Orbit orbit;
    std::vector<float> heights;
    float position = 0.5f, glow = 0.0f;
};

STELLA_ELEMENT (WaveScan, "My oscillator's waves in 3D along its scan knob, the playing row lit; drag to turn it")
```
stella_view3d.h, in `stella::ui::view3d`: `Camera` (`fit (low, high)` each paint; `project (x, y, z)` gives the screen point: x -1..1 across, y up, z -1 front to 1 back), `Orbit` (the mouse), `terrain (g, cam, heights, rows, points, height, floor, lookOf, crossEvery)` (rows of -1..1 heights, row 0 at the front; `crossEvery` 8 adds lines across the rows, a wireframe), `RowLook` (`line`, `thickness`, `glow`, `glowWidth`, `cross`, `xray`), `stage`, `ribbon` (a cheap thick line), `glide`, `clamp`, `colourFrom` (a colour from a setting's text). Rows that change while playing roll back: shift `heights` back by one row and write the new one at the front.

## Steps
1. Read the project first: the parameter ids, the engine each oscillator uses, the module's displays.
2. If the module doesn't show the live values yet, add its displays (`"env"`, and the morph, mix or cutoff with its modulation) and `build`.
3. Place the displays with `edit_layout` as above, bound to the real ids and displays.

Tell the user in plain words: "Your oscillator now has a 3D screen: the wave that plays lights up and glows as you play. Drag it to turn it."
