// D:\workspace\Fanan_web_hub\src\Track.h

#pragma once

#include <juce_audio_basics/juce_audio_basics.h>

#include "AnalogBoard.h"
#include "AudioMedia.h"
#include "Choir.h"
#include "LiveShow.h"
#include "Automation.h"
#include "EffectChain.h"
#include "MidiFx.h"
#include "Sequence.h"
#include "Transport.h"
#include "Plugin.h"

#include <array>
#include <atomic>
#include <memory>
#include <tuple>
#include <utility>

//==============================================================================
/**
    One track, of one of two kinds:
      instrument  MIDI clips and live notes, through its MIDI FX, into a sound source
                  (the built-in test synth or a WCLAP instrument);
      audio       audio clips and a live input from the audio device, which it can
                  monitor and record. A choir track is an audio track whose clips sing as a
                  choir as well (its Choir).
    Either way, then a chain of insert effects and the fader settings. Frozen, a render of what
    it feeds its mixer (before the fader) plays in its place. While the song is mixed
    on the Analog Board, its dry sound (before the inserts) goes to its strip there instead. While
    the Live Show plays, a track marked as one of its channels plays there (its input or live
    notes through its inserts), and the others rest.

    The engine owns the tracks. Fader settings are atomics the page may change at
    any time. Plugins are swapped only by the engine, while it holds its graph lock,
    so the audio thread never sees a half-installed plugin.
*/
class Track final
{
public:
    // fx: an FX channel (Studio One's): no clips of its own, it plays what tracks send to it.
    /** A bus is a Console channel the tracks chosen play into (instead of Main or a Sub), mixed
        through its own inserts, fader and pan into its output. Buses don't play into buses. */
    enum class Kind { instrument, audio, fx, bus };

    /** An FX channel or a bus: a channel of the Console, with no clips and no notes. */
    bool isMixChannel() const noexcept          { return kind == Kind::fx || kind == Kind::bus; }

    /** A send: a copy of the track's sound (after its fader) to an FX channel, or to a
        plugin's sidechain input (a compressor ducking under the kick, say). */
    struct Send
    {
        int id = 0;
        bool sidechain = false;
        int target = 0;            // an FX channel's track id; for a sidechain, the channel the plugin is on
        int slot = 0;              // sidechain: 0 the channel's instrument, otherwise an insert's id
        float levelDb = 0.0f;
        bool on = true;
        float lastGain = 0.0f;     // audio thread: where the level's ramp left off
    };

    Track (int id, juce::uint32 colourArgb, Kind kind = Kind::instrument);
    ~Track();

    //==============================================================================
    const int id;
    const Kind kind;
    juce::String name;             // message thread
    bool nameIsAutomatic = true;   // renamed after its instrument until the user names it
    juce::uint32 colour = 0;       // ARGB, message thread

    std::atomic<float> volumeDb { 0.0f };
    std::atomic<float> pan { 0.0f };           // -1 left .. +1 right
    std::atomic<bool> mute { false }, solo { false }, monitor { false }, recordArm { false };
    bool monitorDecided = false;   // Monitor was set by the user, or once by Sonify (an instrument plugin added): Sonify leaves it alone now
    std::atomic<float> peakLeft { 0.0f }, peakRight { 0.0f };

    static constexpr float silentDb = -72.0f;  // at or below this the fader is closed
    static constexpr float maxDb = 10.0f;      // top of the fader, as on Studio One

    //==============================================================================
    // Plugins. Null instrument: the test synth plays. The inserts follow in order. The MIDI FX
    // (instrument tracks) come before the instrument: what it hears goes through them first.
    std::unique_ptr<Plugin> instrument;
    EffectChain inserts;
    MidiFxChain midiFx;

    //==============================================================================
    // Clips. The message thread owns the clips; after a change the engine builds a new
    // Sequence and swaps it in under its graph lock, and the audio thread plays that.
    std::vector<MidiClip> clips;
    std::unique_ptr<const Sequence> sequence;
    Sequencer sequencer;

    //==============================================================================
    // Audio tracks. input is which of the engine's inputs the track hears; inputLeft and
    // inputRight are where that is among the device's active input channels (right -1:
    // mono). A mono input can take more channels (inputAlso, each one up: 0 is none).
    // The channel is stereo or mono (monoMode). Stereo: each of the input's channels on a side
    // of its own (its left on the left, its right on the right; one channel alone on both).
    // Mono: all of them together as one sound, connected to both sides (two same monos), and
    // recorded as one. The playlist is swapped, and the recorder set, under the engine's graph lock.
    static constexpr int maxInputChannels = 8;       // a mono input's channels, at the most
    int input = 0;                                   // message thread
    std::atomic<int> inputLeft { -1 }, inputRight { -1 };
    std::array<std::atomic<int>, maxInputChannels - 1> inputAlso {};
    std::atomic<bool> monoMode { false };

    /** A mono input on more than one channel. */
    bool hearsSeveralInputs() const noexcept
    {
        for (const auto& also : inputAlso)
            if (also.load (std::memory_order_relaxed) > 0)
                return true;

        return false;
    }

    /** Its recordings' channels: two on a stereo channel hearing two or more, else one. */
    int recordingChannels() const noexcept
    {
        return ! monoMode.load() && (inputRight.load() >= 0 || hearsSeveralInputs()) ? 2 : 1;
    }

    std::atomic<float> inputPeakLeft { 0.0f }, inputPeakRight { 0.0f };   // its input as it hears it, each side
    std::unique_ptr<const AudioPlaylist> playlist;
    juce::AudioFormatWriter::ThreadedWriter* recorder = nullptr;

    /** A choir track: an audio track whose clips (its vocal) sing as a choir too (Choir.h). Set
        once, by the engine under its graph lock; its input, while monitored, is heard alone. */
    std::unique_ptr<Choir> choir;
    bool isChoir() const noexcept                    { return choir != nullptr; }

    //==============================================================================
    // Frozen (instrument and audio tracks): its own sound as it feeds its mixer, rendered over
    // the song into frozenFile, plays in place of its clips, instrument, MIDI FX and inserts,
    // which rest (the Live Show still hears its input and notes live). On the Console that's
    // its sound through its inserts; with the Analog Board mixing, its dry sound (frozenDry).
    // frozen is swapped in under the engine's graph lock; the rest is the message thread's.
    std::unique_ptr<const AudioPlaylist> frozen;
    juce::File frozenFile;                           // none: it isn't frozen
    bool frozenDry = false;                          // rendered for the Analog Board (before its inserts)
    TempoMap frozenMap;                              // the song's tempos, signatures and keys it was rendered at
    int contentRevision = 0;                         // counts the changes to what it plays

    /** A track keying a sidechain its render heard, as it sounded then: a send comes after the
        fader, pan and mute (one its automation drives as the song plays: that lane, not the knob). */
    struct KeyLevel
    {
        int id = 0;
        bool mute = false, volumeAutomated = false, panAutomated = false;
        float volumeDb = 0.0f, pan = 0.0f;

        bool operator== (const KeyLevel& other) const noexcept
        {
            return id == other.id && mute == other.mute
                && volumeAutomated == other.volumeAutomated && panAutomated == other.panAutomated
                && (volumeAutomated || juce::exactlyEqual (volumeDb, other.volumeDb))
                && (panAutomated || juce::exactlyEqual (pan, other.pan));
        }
    };

    std::vector<KeyLevel> frozenKeys;                // the tracks keying its render, as they were

    bool isFrozen() const noexcept                   { return frozenFile != juce::File(); }

    //==============================================================================
    // Where it plays (any kind of track): Main, or a Sub output (Song Setup > Audio I/O Setup >
    // Outputs), by the song output's id; 0 is Main. outputSlot is the audio thread's: the Sub's
    // place among the engine's Sub outputs, -1 for Main.
    int output = 0;                                  // message thread
    std::atomic<int> outputSlot { -1 };

    // A bus it plays into instead (its track id; 0: none), for tracks only. While that bus isn't
    // in the song (removed, until an undo brings it back), the track plays into its output.
    std::atomic<int> outputBus { 0 };

    //==============================================================================
    // Automation. The envelopes are the message thread's; the playback copy is swapped in
    // under the engine's graph lock and applied by the audio thread at each block.
    std::vector<AutomationLane> automation;

    // Sends: the message thread's list, and the audio thread's copy (swapped under the graph lock).
    std::vector<Send> sends;
    std::vector<Send> audioSends;
    int nextSendId = 1;

    /** What an FX channel or a bus plays: tracks' sends, or the tracks playing into the bus,
        add into it each block. */
    juce::AudioBuffer<float> busInput;

    // MIDI in: what the track's instrument hears. External devices by name ("Keys"), one
    // channel of a split device ("Keys|3"), MIDI ports no device uses by their own name, and
    // other tracks' plugins that play notes themselves ("track:<id>"). The message thread's
    // list, and the audio thread's resolved copies (swapped under the graph lock).
    juce::StringArray midiInputs;

    /** A MIDI port the track hears, with what of it gets through. */
    struct MidiRoute
    {
        int slot = 0;                    // the port's queue in the engine
        juce::uint16 channels = 0xffff;  // the MIDI channels let through, one bit each (bit 0: channel 1)
        juce::uint8 blocked = 0;         // the kinds of message kept out: Block flags
    };

    enum Block : juce::uint8 { blockAftertouch = 1, blockProgramChange = 2, blockPitchBend = 4, blockControllers = 8 };

    std::vector<MidiRoute> midiRoutes;
    std::vector<int> midiSourceTracks;
    juce::MidiBuffer liveMidi;       // audio thread: this block's notes in

    // MPE: while the track hears an MPE device, its instrument is told so (the MPE configuration
    // and the pitch bend range) in the next block, and again whenever the instrument changes.
    std::atomic<int> mpeRange { 0 };                 // message thread sets it: 0, no MPE device
    std::atomic<bool> mpeResend { false };           // the range changed: tell the instrument again
    const void* mpeToldInstrument = nullptr;         // audio thread: the instrument last told

    /** Its strip on the Analog Board (AnalogBoard.h): instrument and audio tracks have one. */
    AnalogBoard::Strip board;

    /** Its channel on the Live Show's mixer (LiveShow.h), and whether it's one of the show's
        channels (a singer's mic, a player's instrument): instrument and audio tracks. */
    LiveShow::Channel live;
    std::atomic<bool> liveChannel { false };

    int height = 0;                  // its height in the arrangement; 0 follows the view's size
    std::atomic<int> automationMode { static_cast<int> (AutomationMode::read) };
    std::unique_ptr<AutomationPlayback> automationPlayback;

    /** Held notes (and a held sustain pedal) are released in the next block it plays (used when
        the track stops listening, and around a render). */
    void requestNotesOff() noexcept { notesOffRequested.store (true); }

    //==============================================================================
    // Audio side. prepare() runs while no audio callback is active.
    void prepare (double sampleRate, int maxBlockSize);

    /** Plays the clips and the live notes (instrument) or the clips and the live input
        (audio) through the source and the inserts, into the track's own buffer. live is
        empty unless the track is monitoring or armed. inputs are the device's active
        input channels; recording says whether an audio track's recorder takes this block.
        dry: the inserts are left out (the Analog Board mixes the song). hearInput: an audio
        track hears its input even when it isn't monitoring (the Live Show plays it). A frozen
        track plays its render instead, unless hearInput (the show hears it live). */
    void render (const juce::MidiBuffer& liveNotes, const float* const* inputs, int numInputs, bool recording,
                 const Transport& transport, const clap_event_transport_t& position, int numSamples, bool dry = false,
                 bool hearInput = false) noexcept;

    /** The block render() made, and how long it is. */
    const float* getBlock (int channel) const noexcept   { return buffer.getReadPointer (juce::jlimit (0, 1, channel)); }
    int getBlockSamples() const noexcept                 { return renderedSamples; }

    /** Its meters show this block (the Analog Board's strip mixed it). */
    void showLevels (float left, float right) noexcept;

    /** Its inserts play a block of silence (the Analog Board mixing: their tails die away, heard
        nowhere). After render(), whose block it takes. */
    void quietInserts (const clap_event_transport_t& position) noexcept;

    /** Adds the rendered block to the output with the fader settings applied. right may be null. */
    void mixInto (float* left, float* right, int numSamples, bool audible) noexcept;

    /** Adds the block as mixInto() just did (after the fader and pan) to a send's destination,
        at the send's level; lastGain carries the level's ramp between blocks. */
    void sendInto (float* left, float* right, int numSamples, float gain, float& lastGain) const noexcept;

    /** The next block starts at the fader's own setting instead of ramping there from the last
        block's (a mixdown's first block: the song may have been soloed or elsewhere until then). */
    void settleGain (bool audible) noexcept;

private:
    /** Adds a playlist's audio (its clips, or its frozen render) at the song's place. Each item
        ramps in and out over a few samples, so it never clicks; a render made from the song's
        start, as the track played there, comes in as it is (fadeStart false). */
    static void playClips (const AudioPlaylist* list, const Transport& transport, float* left, float* right, bool fadeStart = true) noexcept;

    /** The fader's gain for each side, after the pan (the pan only turns a side down). */
    std::pair<float, float> faderGains (bool audible) const noexcept;

    juce::Synthesiser synth;
    juce::AudioBuffer<float> buffer;
    juce::AudioBuffer<float> inputSum;   // its input's channels added up: one sound (mono), or each side's (stereo from more)
    juce::MidiBuffer notesOffMidi, releaseMidi, blockMidi;
    std::atomic<bool> notesOffRequested { false };
    float lastGainLeft = 0.0f, lastGainRight = 0.0f;
    float rampFromLeft = 0.0f, rampFromRight = 0.0f;   // this block's fader ramp, for the sends
    int renderedSamples = 0;

    JUCE_DECLARE_NON_COPYABLE_WITH_LEAK_DETECTOR (Track)
};

// D:\workspace\Fanan_web_hub\src\Transport.cpp

#include "Transport.h"

#include <cmath>

namespace
{
    constexpr double clickLengthSeconds = 0.06;
    constexpr double clickAttackSeconds = 0.0004;
    constexpr double clickDecaySeconds = 0.010;
    constexpr double accentFrequency = 1500.0;
    constexpr double beatFrequency = 1000.0;

    clap_beattime toBeatTime (double quarterNotes) noexcept
    {
        return static_cast<clap_beattime> (std::llround (quarterNotes * static_cast<double> (CLAP_BEATTIME_FACTOR)));
    }

    clap_sectime toSecTime (double seconds) noexcept
    {
        return static_cast<clap_sectime> (std::llround (seconds * static_cast<double> (CLAP_SECTIME_FACTOR)));
    }
}

//==============================================================================
Transport::Transport()
    : audioMap (std::make_unique<TempoMap>())
{
}

void Transport::setPlaying (bool shouldPlay) noexcept
{
    if (! shouldPlay)
        recordSetting.store (false);   // stopping ends recording

    requestedPlaying.store (shouldPlay ? 1 : 0);
}

void Transport::togglePlaying() noexcept
{
    // A request the audio thread hasn't picked up yet counts as the current state,
    // so two quick toggles cancel out instead of both reading "stopped".
    const auto pending = requestedPlaying.load();
    const bool current = pending >= 0 ? pending == 1 : playingNow.load();
    setPlaying (! current);
}

void Transport::setRecording (bool shouldRecord) noexcept
{
    recordSetting.store (shouldRecord);
}

void Transport::locate (double ppq) noexcept
{
    requestedLocate.store (juce::jmax (0.0, ppq));
}

void Transport::setLoop (bool enabled, double startPpq, double endPpq) noexcept
{
    if (! std::isfinite (startPpq) || ! std::isfinite (endPpq))
        return;

    startPpq = juce::jlimit (0.0, maxPosition - minLoopLength, startPpq);
    endPpq = juce::jlimit (startPpq + minLoopLength, maxPosition, endPpq);

    loopStartSetting.store (startPpq);
    loopEndSetting.store (endPpq);
    loopSetting.store (enabled);
}

void Transport::setMetronome (bool enabled, float volume) noexcept
{
    if (std::isfinite (volume))
        metronomeVolumeSetting.store (juce::jlimit (0.0f, 1.0f, volume));

    metronomeSetting.store (enabled);
}

//==============================================================================
void Transport::setTempoMap (const TempoMap& map)
{
    if (map == songMap)
        return;

    songMap = map;
    auto fresh = std::make_unique<TempoMap> (map);   // made here: nothing allocates under the lock

    {
        const juce::SpinLock::ScopedLockType lock (mapLock);
        std::swap (audioMap, fresh);
        mapGeneration.fetch_add (1);
    }
}   // the old copy goes here, outside the lock

void Transport::setTempo (double bpm)
{
    if (std::isfinite (bpm))
        setTempoMap (songMap.withTempoAt (positionNow.load(), bpm));
}

void Transport::setTimeSignature (int numerator, int denominator)
{
    if (isValidDenominator (denominator))
        setTempoMap (songMap.withSignatureAt (positionNow.load(), juce::jlimit (1, 32, numerator), denominator));
}

Transport::State Transport::getState() const noexcept
{
    State state;
    state.playing = playingNow.load();
    state.ppq = positionNow.load();
    state.loopEnabled = loopSetting.load();
    state.loopStart = loopStartSetting.load();
    state.loopEnd = loopEndSetting.load();
    state.metronomeEnabled = metronomeSetting.load();
    state.metronomeVolume = metronomeVolumeSetting.load();
    state.recording = recordSetting.load();

    // Where the song is, in the map's terms.
    const auto bar = songMap.barAt (state.ppq);
    state.bpm = songMap.bpmAt (state.ppq);
    state.numerator = bar.numerator;
    state.denominator = bar.denominator;
    state.seconds = songMap.secondsAt (state.ppq);
    state.bar = bar.index;
    state.barStart = bar.start;
    state.barLength = bar.length();
    state.previousBarStart = bar.index > 0 ? songMap.ppqOfBar (bar.index - 1) : 0.0;
    return state;
}

//==============================================================================
void Transport::prepare (double newSampleRate) noexcept
{
    sampleRate = newSampleRate;
    clickSamplesLeft = 0;
    numClicks = 0;
    plannedGeneration = 0xffffffff;   // song time is counted afresh at the new rate
}

void Transport::beginBlock (clap_event_transport_t& out, int numSamples) noexcept
{
    const auto locateTo = requestedLocate.exchange (std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN());
    bool moved = false;

    if (! std::isnan (locateTo))
    {
        position = locateTo;
        moved = true;
    }

    const auto request = requestedPlaying.exchange (-1);

    if (request >= 0)
        playing = request == 1;

    loopEnabled = loopSetting.load();
    loopStart = loopStartSetting.load();
    loopEnd = loopEndSetting.load();
    metronomeEnabled = metronomeSetting.load();
    metronomeVolume = metronomeVolumeSetting.load();
    recording = recordSetting.load();

    playingNow.store (playing);
    positionNow.store (position);

    // The map is borrowed while the block is planned and described: a new one waits until then.
    const juce::SpinLock::ScopedLockType lock (mapLock);
    const auto& map = *audioMap;
    const auto generation = mapGeneration.load();

    // Song time follows the position when it jumps or the map changes (the music stays where it is).
    if (moved || ! playing || generation != plannedGeneration)
    {
        songSample = sampleRate > 0.0 ? static_cast<juce::int64> (std::llround (map.secondsAt (position) * sampleRate)) : 0;
        plannedGeneration = generation;
    }

    planBlock (map, numSamples);
    collectMarks (map);

    // Describe the block start for plugins (tempo-synced effects, arpeggiators and so on).
    const auto bpm = map.bpmAt (position);
    const auto bar = map.barAt (position);

    out = {};
    out.header.size = static_cast<uint32_t> (sizeof (clap_event_transport_t));
    out.header.time = 0;
    out.header.space_id = CLAP_CORE_EVENT_SPACE_ID;
    out.header.type = CLAP_EVENT_TRANSPORT;
    out.header.flags = 0;

    out.flags = CLAP_TRANSPORT_HAS_TEMPO | CLAP_TRANSPORT_HAS_BEATS_TIMELINE
              | CLAP_TRANSPORT_HAS_SECONDS_TIMELINE | CLAP_TRANSPORT_HAS_TIME_SIGNATURE;

    if (playing)
        out.flags |= CLAP_TRANSPORT_IS_PLAYING;

    if (loopActive())
        out.flags |= CLAP_TRANSPORT_IS_LOOP_ACTIVE;

    out.song_pos_beats = toBeatTime (position);
    out.song_pos_seconds = toSecTime (map.secondsAt (position));
    out.tempo = bpm;

    // A ramp: how much the tempo moves each sample through this block.
    out.tempo_inc = numSegments == 1 && numSamples > 0 ? (map.bpmAt (segments[0].to) - bpm) / numSamples : 0.0;

    out.loop_start_beats = toBeatTime (loopStart);
    out.loop_end_beats = toBeatTime (loopEnd);
    out.loop_start_seconds = toSecTime (map.secondsAt (loopStart));
    out.loop_end_seconds = toSecTime (map.secondsAt (loopEnd));
    out.bar_start = toBeatTime (bar.start);
    out.bar_number = static_cast<int32_t> (bar.index);
    out.tsig_num = static_cast<uint16_t> (bar.numerator);
    out.tsig_denom = static_cast<uint16_t> (bar.denominator);
}

void Transport::endBlock (float* left, float* right, int numSamples) noexcept
{
    if (numSegments > 0)
    {
        position = plannedEnd;
        songSample = plannedEndSample;
    }

    renderClicks (left, right, numSamples);
    positionNow.store (position);
}

//==============================================================================
void Transport::planBlock (const TempoMap& map, int numSamples) noexcept
{
    numSegments = 0;
    numClicks = 0;
    loopSamplesOn = false;
    ppqPerSample = sampleRate > 0.0 ? map.bpmAt (position) / (60.0 * sampleRate) : 0.0;

    if (! playing || ppqPerSample <= 0.0 || numSamples <= 0)
        return;

    const auto looping = loopActive();

    // The loop in samples, as the jump below lands it: back to its start's sample when the song
    // reaches the first sample at or after its end.
    if (looping)
    {
        loopSamplesOn = true;
        loopFromSample = static_cast<juce::int64> (std::llround (map.secondsAt (loopStart) * sampleRate));
        loopToSample = static_cast<juce::int64> (std::ceil (map.secondsAt (loopEnd) * sampleRate - 1.0e-6));
    }

    const auto ppqAtSample = [&map, this] (juce::int64 sample) { return map.ppqAt (static_cast<double> (sample) / sampleRate); };
    auto from = position;
    auto fromSample = songSample;
    int offset = 0;
    int remaining = numSamples;

    // Each segment consumes at least one sample. Even the shortest loop allowed at the
    // fastest tempo fits a normal block in far fewer segments than the cap.
    while (remaining > 0 && numSegments < maxSegments)
    {
        const auto to = ppqAtSample (fromSample + remaining);
        auto& segment = segments[static_cast<size_t> (numSegments++)];

        if (looping && from < loopEnd && to >= loopEnd)
        {
            // The tolerance keeps a distance that is a whole number of samples (in exact
            // arithmetic) from rounding up one sample late.
            const auto loopEndSample = map.secondsAt (loopEnd) * sampleRate;
            const auto toEnd = juce::jlimit (1, remaining, static_cast<int> (std::ceil (loopEndSample - static_cast<double> (fromSample) - 1.0e-6)));
            segment = { from, loopEnd, offset, toEnd, (loopEnd - from) / toEnd, fromSample, static_cast<double> (fromSample) / sampleRate };
            offset += toEnd;
            remaining -= toEnd;
            from = loopStart;
            fromSample = static_cast<juce::int64> (std::llround (map.secondsAt (loopStart) * sampleRate));
        }
        else
        {
            segment = { from, to, offset, remaining, (to - from) / remaining, fromSample, static_cast<double> (fromSample) / sampleRate };
            from = to;
            fromSample += remaining;
            remaining = 0;
        }
    }

    // Out of segments (a pathological loop): the rest of the block continues without jumping.
    if (remaining > 0)
    {
        auto& last = segments[static_cast<size_t> (numSegments - 1)];
        last.length += remaining;
        fromSample = last.sample + last.length;
        from = last.to = ppqAtSample (fromSample);
        last.perSample = (last.to - last.from) / last.length;
    }

    plannedEnd = from;
    plannedEndSample = fromSample;
    ppqPerSample = segments[0].perSample;

    for (int i = 0; i < numSegments; ++i)
        collectClicks (map, segments[static_cast<size_t> (i)]);
}

void Transport::addMark (const TempoMap& map, double ppq, int segment, const TempoMap::Bar& bar, bool barLine) noexcept
{
    if (numMarks >= maxMarks)
        return;

    const auto key = map.keyAt (bar.start);
    auto& mark = marks[static_cast<size_t> (numMarks++)];
    mark.ppq = ppq;
    mark.segment = segment;
    mark.barLine = barLine;
    mark.bar = bar.index;
    mark.barLength = bar.length();
    mark.keyRoot = key.root;
    mark.keyNotes = TempoMap::scaleNotes (key.scale);
    mark.bpm = map.bpmAt (ppq);
}

void Transport::collectMarks (const TempoMap& map) noexcept
{
    numMarks = 0;

    // A position this close before a bar line is on it (the samples' rounding).
    constexpr double near = 1.0e-7;

    if (numSegments == 0)
    {
        const auto bar = map.barAt (position + near);
        addMark (map, position, -1, bar, std::abs (position - bar.start) < near);
        return;
    }

    for (int s = 0; s < numSegments; ++s)
    {
        const auto& segment = segments[static_cast<size_t> (s)];
        auto bar = map.barAt (segment.from + near);
        addMark (map, segment.from, s, bar, std::abs (segment.from - bar.start) < near);

        // The bar lines after its start (marks run out long before a block could reach them).
        while (numMarks < maxMarks)
        {
            const auto next = bar.start + bar.length();

            if (next >= segment.to - near)
                break;

            const auto following = map.barAt (next + near);

            if (following.start < next - 1.0e-6)   // past the last bar the map counts
                break;

            addMark (map, next, s, following, true);
            bar = following;
        }
    }
}

void Transport::collectClicks (const TempoMap& map, const Segment& segment) noexcept
{
    if (! metronomeEnabled || segment.length <= 0 || segment.perSample <= 0.0)
        return;

    // Each beat of each bar the segment touches; the bar's first is the accent.
    auto bar = map.barAt (segment.from);

    while (bar.start < segment.to && numClicks < maxClicksPerBlock)
    {
        const auto beat = bar.beat();

        for (int index = 0; index < bar.numerator && numClicks < maxClicksPerBlock; ++index)
        {
            const auto at = bar.start + index * beat;

            if (at < segment.from - 1.0e-9 || at >= segment.to)
                continue;

            const auto sample = static_cast<int> (std::llround ((at - segment.from) / segment.perSample));
            clicks[static_cast<size_t> (numClicks++)] = { segment.offset + juce::jlimit (0, segment.length - 1, sample), index == 0 };
        }

        const auto next = bar.start + bar.length();
        bar = map.barAt (next);

        if (bar.start < next - 1.0e-6)   // past the last bar the map counts
            break;
    }
}

void Transport::startClick (bool accent) noexcept
{
    clickSamplesLeft = static_cast<int> (clickLengthSeconds * sampleRate);
    clickTime = 0.0;
    clickPhase = 0.0;
    clickPhaseStep = juce::MathConstants<double>::twoPi * (accent ? accentFrequency : beatFrequency) / sampleRate;
    clickGain = metronomeVolume * (accent ? 0.5f : 0.32f);
}

void Transport::renderClicks (float* left, float* right, int numSamples) noexcept
{
    if (numClicks == 0 && clickSamplesLeft <= 0)
        return;

    const auto timeStep = 1.0 / sampleRate;
    int nextClick = 0;

    for (int i = 0; i < numSamples; ++i)
    {
        while (nextClick < numClicks && clicks[static_cast<size_t> (nextClick)].sample == i)
            startClick (clicks[static_cast<size_t> (nextClick++)].accent);

        if (clickSamplesLeft <= 0)
        {
            if (nextClick >= numClicks)
                return;

            continue;
        }

        const auto envelope = (1.0 - std::exp (-clickTime / clickAttackSeconds)) * std::exp (-clickTime / clickDecaySeconds);
        const auto sample = static_cast<float> (clickGain * envelope * std::sin (clickPhase));

        if (left != nullptr)
            left[i] += sample;

        if (right != nullptr && right != left)
            right[i] += sample;

        clickPhase += clickPhaseStep;
        clickTime += timeStep;
        --clickSamplesLeft;
    }
}




--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

// D:\workspace\Fanan_web_hub\src\Transport.h

#pragma once

#include <juce_core/juce_core.h>

#include <clap/clap.h>

#include "TempoMap.h"

#include <array>
#include <atomic>
#include <limits>
#include <memory>

//==============================================================================
/**
    Song position, tempo map, loop, record and metronome.

    The message thread sends requests (play, stop, locate, settings). The audio thread
    applies them at the start of each block and works out which stretches of the song
    the block covers (more than one when it loops back). Tracks play their clips from
    that plan, recording stamps live notes with it, and the metronome clicks on it, so
    all three agree to the sample. Everything the two threads share is atomic, except the
    tempo map, which the audio thread borrows only while it plans a block.

    Positions, the loop included, are in quarter notes (PPQ) from the start of the
    song, so a loop can start and end anywhere on the grid. The tempo map (the song
    channel's tempo changes, ramps and time signatures) turns them into time: while the
    song plays, the transport counts its time in samples, so audio clips (which keep
    their speed) land exactly whatever the tempo does. Bars are counted from 0 inside the
    engine; the page shows them from 1.
*/
class Transport final
{
public:
    //==============================================================================
    /** How the song stands. The musical fields are worked out from the map on the message
        thread: call getState() there. */
    struct State
    {
        bool playing = false;
        double ppq = 0.0;
        double bpm = 120.0;           // the tempo where the song is
        int numerator = 4;            // the time signature of the bar it's in
        int denominator = 4;
        bool loopEnabled = false;
        double loopStart = 0.0;       // where the loop starts, in quarter notes
        double loopEnd = 16.0;        // where it ends (and jumps back to loopStart)
        bool metronomeEnabled = false;
        float metronomeVolume = 0.6f;
        bool recording = false;

        double seconds = 0.0;         // where the song is, in time
        int bar = 0;                  // the bar it's in (from 0), where that starts, and its length
        double barStart = 0.0, barLength = 4.0;
        double previousBarStart = 0.0;
    };

    /** A stretch of song that one block plays without jumping. */
    struct Segment
    {
        double from = 0.0, to = 0.0;     // song positions, quarter notes
        int offset = 0, length = 0;      // where in the block, in samples
        double perSample = 0.0;          // quarter notes a sample, on average across it
        juce::int64 sample = 0;          // song time at its start, in samples
        double seconds = 0.0;            // and in seconds
    };

    static constexpr int maxSegments = 32;

    /** The music at a point of the block (MIDI FX follow it): where a segment starts, and each
        bar line inside it; while stopped, one, where the song stands. */
    struct Mark
    {
        double ppq = 0.0;
        int segment = -1;                // the segment it's in; -1 while stopped
        bool barLine = false;            // a bar starts here
        int bar = 0;                     // the bar it's in (from 0) and that bar's length
        double barLength = 4.0;
        int keyRoot = 0;                 // the key there: 0 C .. 11 B, and its scale's notes
        juce::uint16 keyNotes = 0x0ab5;  // (TempoMap::scaleNotes)
        double bpm = 120.0;
    };

    static constexpr int maxMarks = 96;

    static constexpr double minTempo = TempoMap::minTempo;
    static constexpr double maxTempo = TempoMap::maxTempo;
    static constexpr double minLoopLength = 1.0 / 16.0;   // a 64th note
    static constexpr double maxPosition = 1.0e6;          // quarter notes; far past any song

    Transport();

    //==============================================================================
    // Any thread (normally the message thread)
    void setPlaying (bool shouldPlay) noexcept;
    void togglePlaying() noexcept;
    void locate (double ppq) noexcept;
    void setLoop (bool enabled, double startPpq, double endPpq) noexcept;
    void setMetronome (bool enabled, float volume) noexcept;

    /** Recording happens while playing; stopping ends it. */
    void setRecording (bool shouldRecord) noexcept;

    //==============================================================================
    // Message thread: the song channel's map of tempo and signatures.
    void setTempoMap (const TempoMap& map);
    const TempoMap& getTempoMap() const noexcept               { return songMap; }

    /** The tempo that holds where the song is now (one tempo: the song's), and the time
        signature of the bar it's in, from that signature's change on. */
    void setTempo (double bpm);
    void setTimeSignature (int numerator, int denominator);

    /** Counts up each time the map changes (clips that keep their speed follow it). */
    juce::uint32 getMapGeneration() const noexcept            { return mapGeneration.load(); }

    State getState() const noexcept;

    /** True for the denominators the transport accepts: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 and 32. */
    static bool isValidDenominator (int denominator) noexcept  { return TempoMap::isValidDenominator (denominator); }

    //==============================================================================
    // Audio thread
    void prepare (double sampleRate) noexcept;

    /** Applies pending requests, plans the block, and describes its start for plugins. */
    void beginBlock (clap_event_transport_t& transportForPlugins, int numSamples) noexcept;

    /** The stretches of song this block plays, in order; none while stopped.
        Valid from beginBlock() until endBlock(). */
    int getNumSegments() const noexcept                       { return numSegments; }
    const Segment& getSegment (int index) const noexcept      { return segments[static_cast<size_t> (index)]; }

    /** Quarter notes a sample where the block starts (each segment has its own). */
    double getPpqPerSample() const noexcept                   { return ppqPerSample; }

    /** The bar and key where each segment starts and at each bar line in it, in order (one,
        where the song stands, while stopped). Valid from beginBlock() until endBlock(). */
    int getNumMarks() const noexcept                          { return numMarks; }
    const Mark& getMark (int index) const noexcept            { return marks[static_cast<size_t> (index)]; }
    bool isRecordingNow() const noexcept                      { return playing && recording; }

    /** The loop in song samples while it plays round (start, and end: where it jumps back to
        start), for what reads the song ahead of time (a choir track's voices). False while it
        isn't on or the song is stopped. Valid from beginBlock() until endBlock(). */
    bool getLoopSamples (juce::int64& start, juce::int64& end) const noexcept
    {
        start = loopFromSample;
        end = loopToSample;
        return loopSamplesOn;
    }

    /** Where this block starts in the song (quarter notes, and seconds), playing or not. */
    double getBlockStart() const noexcept                     { return position; }
    double getBlockStartSeconds() const noexcept              { return sampleRate > 0.0 ? static_cast<double> (songSample) / sampleRate : 0.0; }

    /** Moves to where the plan ends and adds the metronome to the output (either may be null). */
    void endBlock (float* left, float* right, int numSamples) noexcept;

private:
    //==============================================================================
    struct Click
    {
        int sample = 0;
        bool accent = false;
    };

    void planBlock (const TempoMap& map, int numSamples) noexcept;
    void collectMarks (const TempoMap& map) noexcept;
    void addMark (const TempoMap& map, double ppq, int segment, const TempoMap::Bar& bar, bool barLine) noexcept;
    void collectClicks (const TempoMap& map, const Segment& segment) noexcept;
    void renderClicks (float* left, float* right, int numSamples) noexcept;
    void startClick (bool accent) noexcept;

    bool loopActive() const noexcept        { return loopEnabled && loopEnd > loopStart; }

    //==============================================================================
    // Requests and settings, written by the message thread
    std::atomic<int> requestedPlaying { -1 };      // -1 none, 0 stop, 1 play
    std::atomic<double> requestedLocate { std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN() };
    std::atomic<bool> loopSetting { false };
    std::atomic<double> loopStartSetting { 0.0 }, loopEndSetting { 16.0 };
    std::atomic<bool> metronomeSetting { false };
    std::atomic<float> metronomeVolumeSetting { 0.6f };
    std::atomic<bool> recordSetting { false };

    // The map: the message thread's own, and the audio thread's copy, swapped under the lock
    // (which the audio thread holds only while it plans a block).
    TempoMap songMap;
    std::unique_ptr<TempoMap> audioMap;
    juce::SpinLock mapLock;
    std::atomic<juce::uint32> mapGeneration { 0 };

    // Published by the audio thread
    std::atomic<bool> playingNow { false };
    std::atomic<double> positionNow { 0.0 };

    // Audio thread only
    double sampleRate = 0.0;
    bool playing = false;
    double position = 0.0;
    juce::int64 songSample = 0;                    // song time where the block starts, in samples
    juce::uint32 plannedGeneration = 0xffffffff;   // the map songSample was worked out with
    bool loopEnabled = false;
    double loopStart = 0.0, loopEnd = 16.0;
    bool metronomeEnabled = false;
    float metronomeVolume = 0.6f;
    bool recording = false;

    std::array<Segment, maxSegments> segments {};
    int numSegments = 0;
    std::array<Mark, maxMarks> marks {};
    int numMarks = 0;
    double ppqPerSample = 0.0;
    double plannedEnd = 0.0;
    juce::int64 plannedEndSample = 0;
    bool loopSamplesOn = false;
    juce::int64 loopFromSample = 0, loopToSample = 0;

    static constexpr int maxClicksPerBlock = 64;
    std::array<Click, maxClicksPerBlock> clicks {};
    int numClicks = 0;

    int clickSamplesLeft = 0;
    double clickTime = 0.0, clickPhase = 0.0, clickPhaseStep = 0.0;
    float clickGain = 0.0f;

    JUCE_DECLARE_NON_COPYABLE_WITH_LEAK_DETECTOR (Transport)
};

// D:\workspace\Fanan_web_hub\src\UiHelpers.h
// From KnobMaker (C:\workspace\knobmaker), unchanged: the same knob editor in both apps.

/*
    UiHelpers.h

    Small shared UI utilities. Header-only, so nothing to add to CMakeLists.
*/

#pragma once

#include <juce_gui_basics/juce_gui_basics.h>

//==============================================================================
/** How many pixels of mouse travel it takes to drag a slider across its whole
    range. One value for the whole app, exposed in the toolbar.

    A function-local static in an inline function gives one instance across
    every translation unit. */
inline int& sliderSensitivityValue() noexcept
{
    static int value = 400;
    return value;
}

inline int getSliderSensitivity() noexcept
{
    return sliderSensitivityValue();
}

inline void setSliderSensitivity (int pixelsForFullRange) noexcept
{
    sliderSensitivityValue() = juce::jlimit (50, 4000, pixelsForFullRange);
}

//==============================================================================
/** Tag a slider with this and configurePanelControls leaves its drag behaviour
    alone, so it goes on tracking the pointer's position along its own track.
    For the ones where clicking a spot and landing on that spot IS the point —
    a transport scrubber, or the control that sets the sensitivity itself. */
inline void keepPointerTracking (juce::Slider& slider)
{
    slider.getProperties().set ("pointerTracking", true);
}

//==============================================================================
/** Hides the pointer while a slider is being dragged, and drops it back onto
    the handle when the button comes up.

    Uses unbounded mouse movement rather than just an invisible cursor, which
    buys a second thing worth having: the drag is no longer stopped by the edge
    of the screen. At 400 pixels for a full range that matters — a full sweep
    can easily need more travel than there is monitor.

    JUCE turns unbounded mode off on release and restores the pointer to where
    the drag began. Component mouse listeners run after the component's own
    mouseUp, so by the time this fires that restore has already happened and the
    move to the handle lands on top of it. */
class SliderDragCursor final : public juce::MouseListener
{
public:
    void mouseDrag (const juce::MouseEvent& e) override
    {
        if (dragging != nullptr)
            return;

        auto* slider = dynamic_cast<juce::Slider*> (e.eventComponent);

        if (slider == nullptr)
            return;

        // Not for the ones you aim rather than turn — a transport scrubber or
        // the sensitivity box. There the pointer IS the control.
        if ((bool) slider->getProperties().getWithDefault ("pointerTracking", false))
            return;

        // A click is not a drag. Waiting for real movement stops the cursor
        // blinking out on every stray press.
        if (e.getDistanceFromDragStart() < 3)
            return;

        dragging = slider;
        e.source.enableUnboundedMouseMovement (true, false);
    }

    void mouseUp (const juce::MouseEvent& e) override
    {
        auto* slider = dragging.getComponent();
        dragging = nullptr;

        if (slider == nullptr)
            return;

        const auto bounds = slider->getLocalBounds().toFloat();

        juce::Point<float> handle = bounds.getCentre();

        if (slider->isHorizontal())
            handle = { slider->getPositionOfValue (slider->getValue()), bounds.getCentreY() };
        else if (slider->isVertical())
            handle = { bounds.getCentreX(), slider->getPositionOfValue (slider->getValue()) };

        // e.source is const here, and setScreenPosition is not. The source is a
        // lightweight handle, so a copy addresses the same device.
        auto source = e.source;
        source.setScreenPosition (slider->localPointToGlobal (handle));
    }

private:
    juce::Component::SafePointer<juce::Slider> dragging;
};

/** One instance for the whole app. Components own their listener lists, so a
    slider being destroyed unhooks itself; this outlives all of them. */
inline SliderDragCursor& sliderDragCursor()
{
    static SliderDragCursor instance;
    return instance;
}

//==============================================================================
/** Applies the panel-control rules to a whole component tree.

    Wheel: sliders and combo boxes stop eating it. By default a Slider treats
    the wheel as a value nudge, which in a scrolling panel is wrong twice over —
    the panel does not scroll, and a value the user never meant to touch quietly
    changes. With it off, Slider::mouseWheelMove falls through to
    Component::mouseWheelMove, which hands the event to the parent, so the wheel
    reaches the Viewport and scrolls it.

    Drag: relative, scaled by the sensitivity. Getting here needs two calls, and
    only both together do anything:

      - setSliderSnapsToMousePosition(false) switches a linear slider off the
        branch that maps the pointer straight onto its own on-screen track. In
        the default snapping branch the widget's width IS the sensitivity, so a
        200px row spanning -180..180 is about two degrees per pixel and no
        setting can help it.
      - setMouseDragSensitivity(n) is then honoured: dragging n pixels moves the
        value across its full range, measured from where the drag began.

    Straight-line arithmetic, no acceleration, no threshold. Velocity mode was
    the wrong answer here — it ignores the sensitivity entirely and runs the
    movement through a sine curve with a dead zone at the bottom, which is what
    made small drags do nothing and quick ones jump a fifth of the range in one
    event.

    Cost of snapping being off: clicking the track no longer teleports the thumb
    to that spot. For an editing panel that is a gain, not a loss.

    Call it at the end of a panel's constructor, and again when the sensitivity
    changes; it walks the whole tree, so rows built by helper functions are
    covered without having to remember each one.

    Deliberately NOT applied to the preview knobs: those are the thing being
    designed, not a menu. */
inline void configurePanelControls (juce::Component& parent)
{
    const int sensitivity = getSliderSensitivity();

    for (auto* child : parent.getChildren())
    {
        if (auto* slider = dynamic_cast<juce::Slider*> (child))
        {
            slider->setScrollWheelEnabled (false);

            // JUCE ignores a listener it already holds, so calling this again
            // on every sensitivity change costs nothing.
            slider->addMouseListener (&sliderDragCursor(), false);

            if (! (bool) slider->getProperties().getWithDefault ("pointerTracking", false))
            {
                slider->setVelocityBasedMode (false);
                slider->setSliderSnapsToMousePosition (false);
                slider->setMouseDragSensitivity (sensitivity);
            }
        }
        else if (auto* combo = dynamic_cast<juce::ComboBox*> (child))
        {
            combo->setScrollWheelEnabled (false);
        }

        configurePanelControls (*child);
    }
}
